title: Main result
body_md:
We prove bounds polynomial in $T$ for TFDP-type algorithms with randomly
sampled forward passes. Let $\pi^k$ be the policy of iteration $k$, greedy for the approximations of
iteration $k-1$, and $G^k:=V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)-\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)$ the gap between its expected cost and the lower bound.
Assume that, at every stage, the set of states has dimension at most $d$ and diameter at
most $D$, that the cuts are $L$-Lipschitz on it, and that the initial lower bounds are within $\bar\ell$ per
remaining stage of the cost-to-go functions (e.g.\@\xspace when the stage losses lie in an interval of width
$\bar\ell$, \cref{sec:rates}).
Then the expected number of iterations with $G^k>T\varepsilon$, an error of $\varepsilon$ per stage, is
$O(T\varepsilon^{-(d+1)})$, with a constant that depends only on $d$, $D$, $L$ and $\bar\ell$ (\cref{cor:uniform}). In the discounted case this number does not depend on
the horizon (\cref{cor:disc}). All constants are explicit (\cref{tab:summary}).

label: eq:intro:potential_bound
title: Proof
body_md:
The proof does not use saturation. It follows the analysis of real-time dynamic
programming (RTDP) \citep{barto1995rtdp} in reinforcement learning: the SDDP forward pass is exactly the
sampling scheme of RTDP, which follows greedy trajectories, drawn from the true transition law, of a policy
built on an optimistic value estimate (here a lower bound on costs). Let $\underline V^{k}_{t}$ be the approximation of the
cost-to-go function $V_t$ at time $t$ after $k$ iterations, $\mathcal{B}_t$ the Bellman operator between times $t$ and
$t+1$, $(\bm{x}^k_t)_{0\le t\le T}$, with $\bm{x}^k_0=x_0$, the states visited by the forward pass of iteration $k$, and
$\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$ the history of the first $k-1$ iterations. Besides the gap, two quantities are tracked: the one-step
Bellman residual $r^k_t:=\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{k-1}_{t+1})-\underline V^{k-1}_{t}$, which is local in time, and the volume
$\Phi^k:=\sum_{t<T}\int(\underline V^{k}_{t}-\underline V^{0}_{t})\,d\mu_t$ gained by the approximations, for a reference probability
measure $\mu_t$ on the states at time $t$ (the normalised Lebesgue measure when the state set is
convex). With exact cuts and an exact forward pass, three facts suffice.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{Gap identity} (\cref{lem:gap}), as in \citet[Lemma~2]{efroni2019tight} for RTDP. The gap equals the
expected sum of the residuals along the path that the algorithm samples, so no particular path needs to be
sampled:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro:gap_identity}
G^k=\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t<T}r^k_t(\bm{x}^k_t)\Bigm|\mathcal{A}_{k-1}\Big].
\end{equation}
\item \emph{Lift} (\cref{lem:lift}). The backward pass lifts $\underline V^{k}_{t}$ by its residual at the trial point;
the approximations being Lipschitz, this pointwise lift is a lift on a ball, hence of the integral:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro:volume_lift}
\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\ \ge\ \Psi_T\Big(\sum_{t<T}r^k_t(\bm{x}^k_t)\Big)
\end{equation}
for an explicit convex function $\Psi_T$.
\item \emph{Bounded potential}. The approximations are nondecreasing and stay below the value functions, so
$0\le\Phi^k\le\sum_{t<T}M_t$ with $M_t\le\sup(V_t-\underline V^{0}_{t})$.
\end{enumerate}
Taking expectations in~(ii), using~(i) and Jensen's inequality, and summing over $k$ with~(iii) gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro:potential_bound}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}\Psi_T(G^k)\ \le\ \sum_{t<T}M_t
\end{equation}
(\cref{thm:master}), from which all the rates follow. In metric state spaces, \citet[App.~F]{domingues2021kernel}
and \citet[Lemma~7.3]{sinclair2020adaptive} already accumulate Lipschitz value updates of this kind over a
covering and over adaptive partitions. We transfer this residual accounting to a general cut oracle:
approximate tightness supplies the local lift, while a fixed upper bound on the cuts bounds the potential. To our knowledge,
no earlier paper applies the RTDP analysis to SDDP or to cutting-plane methods.

label: ass:S
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:S}
For every $t\in[T]$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(S\arabic*),ref=(S\arabic*),nosep]
\item\label{S1} $X_{t-1}$ is compact and, for all $x\in X_{t-1}$ and $\xi\in\Xi_t$,
$\emptyset\ne\mathcal{X}_t(x,\xi)\subset X_t$ (forward invariance); $X_T$ need not be compact ($V_T=0$ on it).
\item\label{S2} (Integrability.)
$\sup_{x\in X_{t-1}}\int\big|\inf_{y\in \mathcal{X}_t(x,\xi)}\ell_t(x,y,\xi)\big|\,\mathbb{P}_t(d\xi)<\infty$.
\item\label{S3} (Measurability.) Measurable selections of the stage problems exist, the approximations
of \cref{sec:algo} are Borel functions of finitely many random parameters (for instance cut coefficients), and all
oracles are Borel functions of their inputs.
\end{enumerate}

label: rem:compare
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compare}
With $\zeta_0=0$, $G^k\le\theta$ implies the guarantees of \citet[eqs.~(5.18)--(5.19)]{lan2022complexity}
(a $\theta$-optimal first-stage solution, since $V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)\ge\mathbb{E}[\ell_1(x_0,\bm{x}^k_1,\bm{\xi}^k_1)+V_1(\bm{x}^k_1)]$),
of \citet[Def.~1]{zhang2022stochastic} (a $\theta$-optimal root-node solution) and of
\citet[Thms.~4.2 and~4.11]{forcier2023trajectory} (a $\theta$-solution and a $\theta$-tight lower bound).
These works bound the first index at which their guarantee holds. That index is at most the first
index with $G^k\le\theta$, hence at most $1+\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta\}$, which our bounds control. Such bounds are of
uniform-PAC type \citep{dann2017unifying}. As in all earlier
results on random sampling, identifying a good iteration requires Monte Carlo estimates of $V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)$, unless one returns a
randomly selected iterate (\cref{cor:anytime}(d)).

label: ass:O
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:O}
For each $t<T$ there are a metric $\operatorname{dist}_t$ on $X_t$, possibly extended (with values in
$[0,+\infty]$), a constant $L_t\ge0$ and a \emph{ceiling} $U_t:X_t\to(-\infty,+\infty]$
such that, for all $k\ge1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(O\arabic*),ref=(O\arabic*),nosep]
\item\label{O1} (Lipschitz) $\underline V^{0}_{t}$ and every cut of index $t$ are Borel and
$L_t$-Lipschitz for $\operatorname{dist}_t$, and $\underline V^{0}_{t}$
is deterministic and bounded.
\item\label{O2} (tightness at the trial point, up to $\gamma$) At $x=\bm{x}^k_t$,
$f^k_t(x)\ge\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{k-1}_{t+1})(x)-\bm{\gamma}^k_t$, where the error
$\bm{\gamma}^k_t\ge0$ is integrable and $\mathcal{A}_k$-measurable.
\item\label{O3} (ceiling) $\underline V^{0}_{t}\le U_t$ and every cut of index $t$ is $\le U_t$ on
$X_t$. Moreover the \emph{potential bound} $M_t:=\sup_{X_t}(\bar U_{t}-\underline V^{0}_{t})$ is finite, where
$\bar U_{t}(x):=\inf_{z\in X_t}\{U_t(z)+L_t\operatorname{dist}_t(x,z)\}$, with $L_t\cdot\infty:=\infty$.
\item\label{O4} (monotone update) $\underline V^{k}_{t}=\max\big(\{\underline V^{k-1}_{t},f^k_t\}\cup\{f'_i\}_{i\in[m]}\big)$ for some $m\ge0$,
where the additional cuts $f'_i$, if any, satisfy~\ref{O1} and~\ref{O3}.
\end{enumerate}

label: lem:VG
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:VG}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item \emph{Convex sets.} If $X_t$ is convex and compact, $\operatorname{dist}_t$ is given by a norm,
$d_t:=\dim\operatorname{aff} X_t$, $D_t\ge\operatorname{diam} X_t$ and $\mu_t$ is the normalised Lebesgue measure of
$\operatorname{aff} X_t$ on $X_t$, then~\eqref{eq:setting:volume_growth} holds with $\kappa_t=1$.
\item \emph{Finite unions of convex sets (mixed-integer states).} If
$X_t=\bigcup_{j\in I_t}K^j$ with $I_t$ finite and each $K^j$ convex and compact,
$\mu_t:=|I_t|^{-1}\sum_j\mu_{K^j}$ with $\mu_{K^j}$ as in~(a), $d_t\ge\max_j\dim\operatorname{aff} K^j$ and
$D_t\ge\max_j\operatorname{diam} K^j$, then~\eqref{eq:setting:volume_growth} holds with $\kappa_t=1/|I_t|$ for $\operatorname{dist}_t$ given by a
norm. If the $K^j$ are pairwise disjoint, it also holds for the extended metric equal to
$\|x-y\|$ when $x,y$ lie in the same $K^j$ and $+\infty$ otherwise; for that metric,~\ref{O1}
only asks for Lipschitz continuity on each piece. For instance,
$X_t=\bigcup_{z\in Z_t}\{z\}\times K_z$ with $Z_t$ finite gives $\kappa_t=1/|Z_t|$.
\item \emph{Finite sets.} If $X_t$ is finite and $\mu_t$ is uniform,~\eqref{eq:setting:volume_growth} holds
with $\kappa_t=1/|X_t|$ and $d_t=0$, for any $\operatorname{dist}_t$.
\end{enumerate}

head: environment
name: Bounds

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) A finite maximum of Borel $L_t$-Lipschitz functions is Borel and $L_t$-Lipschitz. If $f$
is $L_t$-Lipschitz and $f\le U_t$, then $f(x)\le f(z)+L_t\operatorname{dist}_t(x,z)\le U_t(z)+L_t\operatorname{dist}_t(x,z)$
for all $z$, so $f\le\bar U_{t}$. This applies to $\underline V^{0}_{t}$ and to every cut, and~\ref{O4} gives the
monotonicity. 
(ii) $\underline V^{0}_{t}\le\bar U_{t}\le M_t+\sup\underline V^{0}_{t}$ by the definition of the potential bound $M_t$ in~\ref{O3}, so $\bar U_{t}$ is bounded; then use
$|\mathcal{B}_t(W)|\le\sup|\mathcal{B}_t(0)|+\sup|W|$ with $W=\underline V^{k-1}_{t+1}$. (iii) The realised costs of $\pi^k$ are
integrable given $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$ (proof of \cref{lem:gap}), and a policy defined by measurable selections with
integrable costs satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\sum_{s>t}\ell_s\mid\bm{x}_t]\ge V_t(\bm{x}_t)$, by backward induction and
stagewise independence.

label: lem:gap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gap}
Under \cref{ass:S}, let $\underline V^{k-1}_{t}$, $t\le T$, be any bounded approximations as in the measurability condition~\ref{S3}, with
$\underline V^{k-1}_{T}=0$. Then the gap $G^k$
of~\eqref{eq:setting:expected_policy_cost} and the sum $R^k$ of the residuals along the sampled path
\eqref{eq:setting:residuals} satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main:gap_identity}
G^k=\mathbb{E}\big[R^k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}\big]+\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t\in[T]}\bm{e}^k_t\ \Big|\ \mathcal{A}_{k-1}\Big],
\qquad \bm{e}^k_t\in[0,\bm{\gamma}^{F,k}_t],
\end{equation}
where $\bm{e}^k_t:=\ell_t(\bm{x}_{t-1},\bm{x}_t,\bm{\xi}_t)+\underline V^{k-1}_{t}(\bm{x}_t)-\dot{\mathcal{B}}_{t-1}(\underline V^{k-1}_{t};\bm{x}_{t-1},\bm{\xi}_t)$ is the
error of the forward step, with $\dot{\mathcal{B}}_{t-1}$ the value of the stage problem~\eqref{eq:setting:bellman_operator}, and
$(\bm{x}_t,\bm{\xi}_t)=(\bm{x}^k_t,\bm{\xi}^k_t)$. In particular $G^k\le\mathbb{E}[R^k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]+\bm{\Gamma}^F_k$,
with equality for the exact greedy pass. Under \cref{ass:O}, the gap inequality~\eqref{eq:setting:gap_meaning} holds.

name: Gap identity

label: eq:main:one_step_expectation
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal H_{t-1}:=\mathcal{A}_{k-1}\vee\sigma(\bm{\xi}^k_{[t-1]})$. Then $\bm{x}_{t-1}$ is
$\mathcal H_{t-1}$-measurable and lies in $X_{t-1}$ by~\ref{S1}, and $\bm{\xi}_t$ is independent of
$\mathcal H_{t-1}$ with law $\mathbb{P}_t$. The substitution (``freezing'') property of independent variables
\citep{kallenberg2002foundations} states that if $g$ is jointly measurable, $Y$ is $\mathcal H$-measurable, $\bm{\xi}$ is
independent of $\mathcal H$ and $\mathbb{E}|g(Y,\bm{\xi})|<\infty$, then $\mathbb{E}[g(Y,\bm{\xi})\mid\mathcal H]=\bar g(Y)$ with
$\bar g(y):=\mathbb{E} g(y,\bm{\xi})$. It gives
$\mathbb{E}[\dot{\mathcal{B}}_{t-1}(\underline V^{k-1}_{t};\bm{x}_{t-1},\bm{\xi}_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]=\mathcal{B}_{t-1}(\underline V^{k-1}_{t})(\bm{x}_{t-1})=\underline V^{k-1}_{t-1}(\bm{x}_{t-1})+r^k_{t-1}(\bm{x}_{t-1})$,
so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main:one_step_expectation}
\mathbb{E}\big[\ell_t(\bm{x}_{t-1},\bm{x}_t,\bm{\xi}_t)+\underline V^{k-1}_{t}(\bm{x}_t)\,\big|\,\mathcal H_{t-1}\big]
=\underline V^{k-1}_{t-1}(\bm{x}_{t-1})+r^k_{t-1}(\bm{x}_{t-1})+\mathbb{E}[\bm{e}^k_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}] .
\end{equation}
Take $\mathbb{E}[\cdot\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]$ and sum over $t\in[T]$. The terms in $\underline V^{k-1}_{}$ telescope to $-\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)$,
because $\underline V^{k-1}_{T}=0$ and $x_0$ is deterministic. The bounds on $\bm{e}^k_t$ are the forward-error condition~\eqref{eq:setting:forward_error}
and the definition of $\dot{\mathcal{B}}_{t-1}$. All terms are integrable given $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$: the realised cost satisfies
$\inf_y\ell_t(\bm{x}_{t-1},y,\bm{\xi}_t)\le\ell_t(\bm{x}_{t-1},\bm{x}_t,\bm{\xi}_t)\le\inf_y\ell_t(\bm{x}_{t-1},y,\bm{\xi}_t)+2\sup|\underline V^{k-1}_{t}|+\bm{\gamma}^{F,k}_t$,
and $\mathbb{E}\big[|\inf_y\ell_t(\bm{x}_{t-1},y,\bm{\xi}_t)|\,\big|\,\mathcal H_{t-1}\big]$ is at most $\sup_{x\in X_{t-1}}\int|\inf_y\ell_t(x,y,\xi)|\,\mathbb{P}_t(d\xi)$,
which is finite by the integrability condition~\ref{S2}, by the freezing property. For the gap inequality~\eqref{eq:setting:gap_meaning}: $G^k\ge V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)-\bar U_{0}(x_0)$ and $\bar U_{0}(x_0)=U_0(x_0)$
because $X_0=\{x_0\}$, so $G^k\ge V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)-V_0(x_0)-\zeta_0$ with $\zeta_0$ as in \cref{sec:accuracy}; and $V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)\ge V_0(x_0)$ by
\cref{lem:basic}(iii).

label: lem:dbp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dbp}
Let $(Y_k)_{k\ge0}$ be adapted to $(\mathcal{A}_k)$ and nonincreasing, with $0\le Y_k\le Y_0=C$ and $C$
deterministic, and let $\mathrm{Reg}_K:=\sum_{k\in[K]}(Y_{k-1}-\mathbb{E}[Y_k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}])$. For $\delta\in(0,1]$, with
probability at least $1-\delta$, $\mathrm{Reg}_K\le9C\ln(3/\delta)$ for all $K$. In particular, if
$\mathbb{E}[Y_{k-1}-Y_k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]\ge f_k\ge0$ with $f_k$ $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$-measurable, then, since
$\mathrm{Reg}_K\ge\sum_{k\in[K]}f_k$, $\sum_{k\ge1}f_k\le9C\ln(3/\delta)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

name: Decreasing bounded processes

label: thm:master
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:master}
Let \cref{ass:S,ass:O} hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item \emph{Volume version.} If~\eqref{eq:setting:volume_growth} holds for all $t<T$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main:master_volume}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}\Psi_T\big((G^k-\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_k)_+\big)\ \le\ \sum_{t<T}\int(\bar U_{t}-\underline V^{0}_{t})\,d\mu_t
\ \le\ \sum_{t<T}M_t .
\end{equation}
In particular, with deterministic errors, $\mathbb{E}\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma\}\le\sum_{t<T}M_t/\Psi_T(\theta)$
for every $\theta>0$. Moreover, for every $\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
simultaneously for all $\theta>0$,
$\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_k\}\le9\ln(3/\delta)\sum_{t<T}M_t/\Psi_T(\theta)$.
\item \emph{Covering version.} Assume deterministic errors $\gamma_t$, $\gamma^F_t$. Fix $\theta>0$, numbers
$\sigma_t\ge0$ with $\sum_{t<T}L_t\sigma_t\le\theta/4$, and finite $\sigma_t$-nets $C_t\subset X_t$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main:master_covering}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}\big(G^k-\Gamma-\theta/2\big)_+\ \le\ \sum_{t<T}\sum_{c\in C_t}(\bar U_{t}-\underline V^{0}_{t})(c)\ \le\ \sum_{t<T}|C_t|\,M_t .
\end{equation}
In particular, $\mathbb{E}\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma\}\le\frac2\theta\sum_{t<T}|C_t|M_t$. Moreover, for every
$\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma\}\le\frac{18\ln(3/\delta)}{\theta}\sum_{t<T}|C_t|M_t$.

\item \emph{Finite state sets.} Assume deterministic errors, every $X_t$ finite and $\operatorname{dist}_t=+\infty$ off the
diagonal. Then
$\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}(G^k-\Gamma)_+\le C_{\rm fin}:=\sum_{t<T}\sum_{x\in X_t}(U_t-\underline V^{0}_{t})(x)$ and, for every
$\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\sum_{k\ge1}(G^k-\Gamma)_+\le9\ln(3/\delta)\,C_{\rm fin}$.
\end{enumerate}

name: Master theorem

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Phi^k:=\sum_{t<T}\int(\underline V^{k}_{t}-\underline V^{0}_{t})\,d\mu_t$ and $C_U:=\sum_{t<T}\int(\bar U_{t}-\underline V^{0}_{t})\,d\mu_t$. By
\cref{lem:basic}(i), $0=\Phi^0\le\Phi^{k-1}\le\Phi^k\le C_U\le\sum_{t<T}M_t$.

\emph{Pathwise lift.} Fix $k\ge1$ and $t<T$, let $x=\bm{x}^k_t$, and let
$s_t:=(r^k_t(x)-\bm{\gamma}^k_t)_+$. As noted after \cref{lem:lift},
$\int(\underline V^{k}_{t}-\underline V^{k-1}_{t})\,d\mu_t\ge\kappa_t\varphi_t(s_t)\ge\psi_t(s_t)$. Sum over $t<T$. By the
definition of $\square$, by $\sum_{t<T}(a_t)_+\ge(\sum_{t<T}a_t)_+$ and because $\Psi_T$ is nondecreasing,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main:pathwise_lift}
\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\ \ge\ \sum_{t<T}\psi_t(s_t)\ \ge\ \Psi_T\Big(\sum_{t<T}s_t\Big)\ \ge\ \Psi_T\big((R^k-\bm{\Gamma}_k)_+\big).
\end{equation}

\emph{Conditional expectation.} The map $(u,v)\mapsto\Psi_T((u-v)_+)$ is convex and finite on
$\mathbb{R}^2$, $R^k$ is bounded by \cref{lem:basic}(ii), and $\bm{\Gamma}_k$ is integrable. The
conditional Jensen inequality, \cref{lem:gap} and monotonicity give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main:conditional_lift}
\mathbb{E}[\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]\ \ge\ \Psi_T\big((\mathbb{E}[R^k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]-\mathbb{E}[\bm{\Gamma}_k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}])_+\big)
\ \ge\ \Psi_T\big((G^k-\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_k)_+\big)=:f_k .
\end{equation}
Summing over $k\in[K]$, the left-hand sides add up to $\mathbb{E}\Phi^K\le C_U$; let $K\to\infty$ (monotone convergence).

\emph{High probability.} \Cref{lem:dbp} applies to $Y_k:=C_U-\Phi^k$, which is adapted by~\ref{S3}, with
$Y_0=C_U$ deterministic since $\underline V^{0}_{}$, the envelopes $\bar U_{t}$ and the measures $\mu_t$ are, and to $f_k$, which
is $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$-measurable. It gives $\sum_{k\ge1}f_k\le9C_U\ln(3/\delta)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, and
$\sum_kf_k\ge\Psi_T(\theta)\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_k\}$ for every $\theta$. The last claim follows
from~\eqref{eq:main:master_volume}, since $\Psi_T$ is nondecreasing.

label: cor:anytime
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:anytime}
In the setting of \cref{thm:master}(a):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item If $\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_k\le g_k$ for a deterministic sequence $(g_k)_{k\ge1}$, then for all
$\theta_1,\theta_2>0$,
$\mathbb{E}\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta_1+\theta_2\}\le\#\{k\ge1:g_k>\theta_2\}+\sum_{t<T}M_t/\Psi_T(\theta_1)$.
\item With deterministic errors, let $K_\theta:=9\ln(3/\delta)\sum_{t<T}M_t/\Psi_T(\theta)$. With
probability at least $1-\delta$, for every $\theta>0$, $V_0(x_0)-\underline V^{k}_{0}(x_0)\le\theta+\Gamma$ at every iteration
$k\ge K_\theta$, and one of the policies
$(\pi^k)_{1\le k\le\lfloor K_\theta\rfloor+1}$ is $(\theta+\Gamma+\zeta_0)$-optimal, with $\zeta_0$ as in \cref{sec:accuracy}.
\item (Almost sure convergence.) With deterministic errors, $\limsup_kG^k\le\Gamma$ almost surely. In particular, with
exact cuts, an exact forward pass and $U=V$, $G^k\to0$ almost surely: the lower bound $\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)$ and the expected
cost $V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)$ of the policy both converge to $V_0(x_0)$.
\item (Uniformly selected iterate; no estimate of $G^k$ is needed.) For $K\ge1$ and $\theta>0$, if $\mathbf k$ is uniform on $[K]$ and independent
of the run, then
$\mathbb{P}(G^{\mathbf k}>\theta+\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_{\mathbf k})\le\sum_{t<T}M_t/(K\Psi_T(\theta))$; on the complementary event,
$\pi^{\mathbf k}$ is $(\theta+\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_{\mathbf k}+\zeta_0)$-optimal and
$V_0(x_0)-\underline V^{\mathbf k-1}_{0}(x_0)\le\theta+\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_{\mathbf k}$.
\end{enumerate}

name: Anytime guarantee

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) If $g_k\le\theta_2$ and $G^k>\theta_1+\theta_2$, the $k$-th term of~\eqref{eq:main:master_volume} is at
least $\Psi_T(\theta_1)$. (b) On the event of \cref{thm:master}, at most $K_\theta$ indices $k$ have
$G^k>\theta+\Gamma$, so some $k\le\lfloor K_\theta\rfloor+1$ has $G^k\le\theta+\Gamma$; use the gap inequality~\eqref{eq:setting:gap_meaning} and

title: Proof

Increasing $D_t$ only weakens~\eqref{eq:setting:volume_growth}, so we may take $D_t=D$.

$\sum_{t<T}M_t\le\bar\ell/(1-\beta)^2$.

label: lem:gapIH
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gapIH}
Under \cref{ass:Sinf}, let $\underline V^{k-1}$ be bounded, let $(\bm{x}_t)_{t\ge0}$ be the trajectory of $\pi^k$ from $x_0$
driven by i.i.d.\ noise independent of $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$, $\lambda_t:=\ell(\bm{x}_t,\bm{x}_{t+1},\bm{\xi}_{t+1})$, and
$e_t:=\lambda_t+\beta\underline V^{k-1}(\bm{x}_{t+1})-\dot{\mathcal{B}}(\underline V^{k-1};\bm{x}_t,\bm{\xi}_{t+1})\in[0,\gamma^F_k]$ the forward error. For every $H\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inf:gap_identity}
G^k=\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\Big[\sum_{t<H}\beta^t\big(r^k(\bm{x}_t)+e_t\big)\Big]+\varepsilon^k_H,\qquad
\varepsilon^k_H\le\beta^H\Big(\frac{\bar\ell}{1-\beta}-\inf_X\underline V^{k-1}\Big),
\end{equation}
where $\varepsilon^k_H:=\mathbb{E}_{k-1}[\sum_{t\ge H}\beta^t\lambda_t]-\beta^H\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\underline V^{k-1}(\bm{x}_H)$ is what a pass of length
$H$ misses. Hence $G^k=\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\sum_{t\ge0}\beta^t(r^k(\bm{x}_t)+e_t)$, and, if $\tau\in\mathbb N^*$ is independent of the path
given $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$, with $\mathbb{P}(\tau>t\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1})=\beta^t$ for all $t\ge0$, then exactly $G^k=\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\big[\sum_{t<\tau}(r^k(\bm{x}_t)+e_t)\big]$.

label: thm:master-ih
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:master-ih}
Let \cref{ass:Sinf,ass:Oinf} hold, and run variant~(G).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]
\item \emph{Volume version.} If~\eqref{eq:setting:volume_growth} holds on $X$ as in \cref{lem:pass}, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inf:master_volume}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}\kappa\,\hat\psi\big((1-\beta)(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+\big)\ \le\ \bar M_U\ \le\ M_U .
\end{equation}
In particular, if $\Gamma^\beta_k\le\Gamma^\beta$ for a deterministic $\Gamma^\beta$, then, for every $\theta>0$,
$\mathbb{E}\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta\}\le\bar M_U/(\kappa\hat\psi((1-\beta)\theta))$, which equals
$2(d+1)\bar M_U\hat\rho^d/(\kappa(1-\beta)^{d+1}\theta^{d+1})$ when $(1-\beta)\theta\le\hat\rho$.
Moreover, for every $\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously for all $\theta>0$,
$\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta_k\}\le9\ln(3/\delta)\,\bar M_U/(\kappa\hat\psi((1-\beta)\theta))$.
\item \emph{Covering version.} Fix $\theta>0$, $\sigma\ge0$ with $4\hat L\sigma\le(1-\beta)\theta$, and a finite
$\sigma$-net $C$ of $X$ for $\operatorname{dist}$, and let $M_C:=\sum_{c\in C}(\bar U-\underline V^{0})(c)\le|C|M_U$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:inf:master_covering}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}\big(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k-\theta/2\big)_+\ \le\ \frac{M_C}{1-\beta}.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\mathbb{E}\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta_k\}\le2M_C/((1-\beta)\theta)$. Moreover, for every
$\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta_k\}\le18\ln(3/\delta)\,M_C/((1-\beta)\theta)$.
\item \emph{Finite state sets.} If $X$ is finite and $\operatorname{dist}=+\infty$ off the diagonal, then
$\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+\le C_{\rm fin}/(1-\beta)$, with $C_{\rm fin}:=\sum_{x\in X}(U-\underline V^{0})(x)$. Moreover,
for every $\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$\sum_{k\ge1}(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+\le9\ln(3/\delta)\,C_{\rm fin}/(1-\beta)$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md:
By the standard argument (convex combinations of $\epsilon$-optimal points stay feasible by graph convexity),
$h=\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{k}_{t+1})$ is convex on the convex set $X^\eta_t$. By induction, every cut of index $t+1$ is valid on
$X_{t+1}$, so $\underline V^{0}_{t+1}\le\underline V^{k}_{t+1}\le V_{t+1}$ there (\cref{lem:valid}(a)). Since $\mathcal{X}_{t+1}(z,\xi)\subset X_{t+1}$
for $z\in X^\eta_t$, monotonicity and~\ref{S2} on $X^\eta_t$ give, on $X^\eta_t$,
$-\infty<\mathcal{B}_t(0)+\inf\underline V^{0}_{t+1}\le h\le\mathcal{B}_t(V_{t+1})=V_t\le\sup_{X^\eta_t}\mathcal{B}_t(0)+\sup_{X_{t+1}}V_{t+1}<\infty$.
Moreover $h\ge\underline V^{k}_{t}\ge\underline V^{0}_{t}$ on $X_t$ by the sub-Bellman inequality. For $x\in X_t$, $X^\eta_t$ contains a relative
neighbourhood of $x$ in $\operatorname{aff} X_t$, so the relative subdifferential is nonempty. The subgradient inequality gives
validity on $X^\eta_t$, and tightness holds by construction. For a unit vector $u$ in the direction space of
$\operatorname{aff} X_t$, $h(x+\eta u)\ge h(x)+\eta\langle g,u\rangle$, so $\langle g,u\rangle\le(\sup_{X^\eta_t}V_t-\inf_{X_t}\underline V^{0}_{t})/\eta$.
Since $\pm u$ are both admissible, $f^k_t$ is $L_t$-Lipschitz on $X_t$. Under the bounded-loss condition,
the same upper bound on $V_t$ and backward induction give $\sup_{X^\eta_t}V_t\le\sum_{s>t}(a_s+\bar\ell)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The setting satisfies~\ref{O1},~\ref{O2} (\cref{lem:valid}(b)),~\ref{O3} with $U_t=V_t$ (\cref{lem:valid}(a))
and~\ref{O4}. Condition~\ref{S3} holds under TFDP's normal-integrand assumptions if the cut oracle is a Borel
function of its inputs: the cuts are then Lipschitz and Borel in finitely many random parameters (the trial points
and noises drawn so far), and $V_{t+1}$ is Lipschitz (\cref{app:measurability}). With random node selection from the
law of $\bm{\xi}_t$, the forward noise has the law used in the Bellman operators, even without finite support. Since
$V_t$ is $\tilde L_t$-Lipschitz \citep[Assumption~3(ii)]{forcier2023trajectory}, we have, at $x=\bm{x}^1_t$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appB:tfdp_initial_gap}
\sup_{X_t}(V_t-\underline V^{1}_{t})\le(V_t-\underline V^{1}_{t})(x)+(\tilde L_t+L_t)D_t
\le\sup_{X_{t+1}}(V_{t+1}-\underline V^{1}_{t+1})+\gamma_t+(\tilde L_t+L_t)D_t ,
\end{equation}
using $\underline V^{1}_{t}(x)\ge\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{1}_{t+1})(x)-\gamma_t$ and $V_t(x)-\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{1}_{t+1})(x)\le\sup(V_{t+1}-\underline V^{1}_{t+1})$.
So $M^{(1)}_t:=\sup(V_t-\underline V^{1}_{t})\le\sum_{t\le s<T}(\gamma_s+(\tilde L_s+L_s)D_s)$, which is deterministic. The

label: rem:AL
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:AL}
An augmented Lagrangian cut $g^{\mathrm{AL}}(b_0;\lambda,\varrho)+\lambda^\top(b_0-b)-\varrho\|b_0-b\|$ of a nodal
value function $g$ at the trial state $b_0$, with multiplier $\lambda$, penalty $\varrho$ and augmented Lagrangian
dual function $g^{\mathrm{AL}}$ \citep[Def.~3]{ahmed2022sldp}, is valid for $g$ (weak duality), is
$(\|\lambda\|_*+\varrho)$-Lipschitz, and is tight if and only if $g^{\mathrm{AL}}(b_0;\lambda,\varrho)=g(b_0)$.
Uniformly Lipschitz cuts require restricting the dual to $\|\lambda\|_*+\varrho\le L_t$. The restricted dual value
is at least $\inf_b\{g(b)+L_t\|b-b_0\|\}$, which equals $g(b_0)$ when $L_t\ge\operatorname{Lip}(g)$ on the whole domain of $g$ \citep[p.~768]{ahmed2022sldp};
the cut then satisfies \cref{ass:O} with $\gamma=0$ and $U=V$. Otherwise the cut is tight only for a
Lipschitz-regularised operator, the setting of \cref{sec:ZS} with a norm regularisation. With SLDP's unregularised
forward pass,~\ref{O2} is then guaranteed only with $\gamma_t$ equal to a regularisation gap, which is not
controlled a priori. \citet{fullner2024lipschitz} study Lipschitz regularisation and the tightness of Lagrangian
cuts in this setting.

title: Proof
body_md:

label: prop:ZSgeneral
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ZSgeneral}
In the setting of \cref{thm:ZS}, without the assumptions on Lipschitz constants, diameters and costs, let $L_s$ be
the Lipschitz constant of the approximations of index $s$ (\cref{prop:ZS}), let $X_s\subset\bigcup_{j\le J_s}B_{s,j}$
with balls of diameters $D_{s,j}$, and let $I_s(\varepsilon_s):=\sum_{j\le J_s}(1+2L_sD_{s,j}/\varepsilon_s)^{d_s}$.
Put $M_0:=v^{\mathrm{prim}}$, the optimal value, and $M_s:=\sup_{x\in X_s}\inf_{z\in X_s}\{V_s(z)+L_s\|x-z\|\}$.
Then, for all $(\varepsilon_s)_{1\le s<T}\subset(0,\infty)$ with $\sum_s\varepsilon_s\le\varepsilon/4$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appB:zs_bound}
\mathbb{E}[\iota]\ \le\ \frac2\varepsilon\Big(M_0+\sum_{s=1}^{T-1}I_s(\varepsilon_s)\,M_s\Big),
\end{equation}
and, for $\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$\iota\le\frac{18\ln(3/\delta)}{\varepsilon}\big(M_0+\sum_sI_s(\varepsilon_s)M_s\big)$. The same bounds
hold for the number of iterations at which the regularised policy is not $\varepsilon$-optimal for the
regularised problem, or the lower bound is not $\varepsilon$-tight.

title: Proof
body_md:
Zhang and Sun's oracles are random functions measurable with respect to $\sigma$-fields $\Sigma^{\rm oracle}_i$. We
assume the sampled paths independent of $\Sigma^{\rm oracle}_\infty$ and include $\Sigma^{\rm oracle}_\infty$ in
$\mathcal{A}_0$, so that the oracle randomness meets the requirement of \cref{sec:algo}. By \cref{prop:ZS},
\cref{thm:master}(b) applies to the regularised problem, with $G^k$ the regularised policy cost minus the lower bound,
also with several paths per iteration (\cref{sec:variants}). By their Assumption~2,
$U_0(x_0)=v^{\mathrm{prim}}=v^{\mathrm{reg}}=V^R_0(x_0)$, so $\zeta_0=0$. Hence $G^k\le\varepsilon$ implies: the
regularised policy has cost at most $v^{\mathrm{reg}}+\varepsilon$; its root decision satisfies their Def.~1; and
$v^{\mathrm{prim}}-\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)\le\varepsilon$. So
$\iota\le\min\{k\ge1:G^k\le\varepsilon\}-1\le\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\varepsilon\}$ (their iteration $i+1$ is our iteration
$k=i+1$). Take the net $\{x_0\}$ of $X_0$, with $M_0=U_0(x_0)=v^{\mathrm{prim}}$ since $\underline V^{0}_{}=0$, and, for
$1\le s<T$, $\sigma_s:=\varepsilon_s/L_s$ if $L_s>0$ and $\sigma_s:=\max_jD_{s,j}$ if $L_s=0$, so that
$2\sum_{s<T}L_s\sigma_s\le2\sum_s\varepsilon_s\le\varepsilon/2$. If $L_s>0$, a maximal $\sigma_s$-separated subset of
$X_s\cap B_{s,j}$ has at most $(1+2D_{s,j}/\sigma_s)^{d_s}$ points, by the packing argument of \cref{lem:nets}(a); if
$L_s=0$, one point of each nonempty $X_s\cap B_{s,j}$ suffices. In both cases $X_s$ has a $\sigma_s$-net of size at
most $I_s(\varepsilon_s)$, and $M_s$ is the potential bound of~\ref{O3} with $U=V$ (under \cref{lem:ZSreg}, it may be
replaced by $\sup_{X_s}V^R_s$). This proves \cref{prop:ZSgeneral}. For the explicit bounds, $M_0\le T\bar\ell$ and
$\sum_{1\le s<T}M_s\le\bar\ell\,T(T-1)/2$, so, at an accuracy $\theta$ and with $I:=\max_sI_s(\varepsilon_s)$,
$\mathbb{E}[\iota]\le(2/\theta)\big(T\bar\ell+I\bar\ell\,T(T-1)/2\big)\le I\bar\ell\,T(T+1)/\theta$. For $\varepsilon$-optimality, take
$\theta=\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon_s=\varepsilon/(4(T-1))$, so $I=(1+8LD(T-1)/\varepsilon)^d$; this
is~\eqref{eq:inst:zs_bound_uniform}. For the accuracy $T\varepsilon$ of \cref{tab:summary}, take $\theta=T\varepsilon$
and $\varepsilon_s=T\varepsilon/(4(T-1))\ge\varepsilon/4$, so $I\le(1+8LD/\varepsilon)^d$ and
$\mathbb{E}[\iota]\le\bar\ell\,(T+1)(1+8LD/\varepsilon)^d/\varepsilon$, linear in $T$.

label: rem:likelihood
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:likelihood}
If the forward noise is drawn from $q_t$ instead of the transition law $p_t$, with $p_t\le\upsilon_tq_t$, the lifts
are obtained along $q$-paths while $G^k$ is a $p$-expectation. Since $(r^k_t)_+\ge0$, the expectation under $p$ of
the positive residuals is at most $\Upsilon:=\prod_{s<T-1}\upsilon_s$ times that under $q$, and the proof of
\cref{thm:master} gives $\mathbb{E}\sum_k\Psi_T(G^k/\Upsilon)\le\sum_{t<T}M_t$ (exact cuts). Under the uniform Assumption~4
of Zhang and Sun, $\upsilon_s=N_s\max p_{nm}$ over the nodes $n$ of stage $s$, each with $N_s$ children $m$, so
$\Upsilon$ is exponential in $T$ unless the transitions are nearly uniform.

name: Monotone step cuts

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\underline V^{0}_{}=0$, losses are nonnegative and $v\le\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{k}_{t+1})(x)\le\bar\ell+\sup\underline V^{k}_{t+1}$, backward induction
gives $0\le\underline V^{k}_{t}\le(T-t)\bar\ell$ on $\mathbb{R}^{n_t}$. \Cref{lem:gap} uses nothing beyond boundedness, so it holds. Fix $k\ge1$,
$t<T$, $x=\bm{x}^k_t$ and $r_t=r^k_t(x)$. On the box $Q:=\{y:x\le y<x+\omega\mathbf 1\}\subset X^+_t$, $f^k_t(y)=v$ and
$\underline V^{k-1}_{t}(y)\le\underline V^{k-1}_{t}(x)$, because $\underline V^{k-1}_{t}$ is nonincreasing. Hence
$\underline V^{k}_{t}(y)-\underline V^{k-1}_{t}(y)\ge v-\underline V^{k-1}_{t}(x)\ge(r_t-\gamma_t)_+$ on $Q$, using $\underline V^{k}_{t}\ge\underline V^{k-1}_{t}$. Since
$\operatorname{vol}(Q)=\omega^{n_t}$, the potential $\Phi^k:=\sum_{t<T}\int_{X^+_t}\underline V^{k}_{t}$ satisfies
$\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\ge\sum_{t<T}\omega^{n_t}(r_t-\gamma_t)_+$ and $\Phi^k\le\bar\ell\sum_{t<T}(T-t)\operatorname{vol}(X^+_t)$. Normalise
stage $t$ by $\omega^{n_t}$ and proceed as in the proof of \cref{thm:master}(c). For the last claim, let
$\zeta_t:=\sup_k\sup_{X_t}(\underline V^{k}_{t}-V_t)_+$. Then $v\le\mathcal{B}_t(V_{t+1}+\zeta_{t+1})(x)=V_t(x)+\zeta_{t+1}$. If $y\in X_t$
and $y<x+\omega\mathbf 1$, then $z:=y\vee x\in X_t$ (box), $z\ge y$ and $\|z-x\|_\infty<\omega$, so
$V_t(y)\ge V_t(z)\ge V_t(x)-\varepsilon$ and $f(y)\le V_t(y)+\varepsilon+\zeta_{t+1}$ for a step cut $f$; elsewhere
$f=0\le V_t$. Hence $\zeta_t\le\varepsilon+\zeta_{t+1}$, and $\zeta_T=0$; this is the minimisation form of
\citet[Lemma~6]{philpott2020midas}. Finally, \cref{lem:gap} gives $V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)-V_0(x_0)\le G^k+\zeta_0$.

label: rem:linexact
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:linexact}
For linear stages with finite optimal values, data affine in $\xi$, a deterministic full-row-rank recourse matrix and
a density of $\mathbb{P}_{t+1}$ that is polynomial on each cell of a polyhedral subdivision of a polytope $\Xi_{t+1}$, the
expectations of \cref{prop:expbenders} are finite sums of integrals of polynomials over polytopes, computable exactly for rational data
\citep{baldoni2011integrate}. Indeed, for fixed $x$, the noises for which a given basis is optimal form a polytope, on
which the value and the subgradient given by the dual solution are polynomials of degree at most two in $\xi$;
conclude by inclusion--exclusion over these polytopes and the density cells. TFDP
\citep[Thm.~3.7]{forcier2023trajectory} builds a stronger exact cut in a related setting.

label: prop:jensen
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:jensen}
Fix $t<T$. Assume that $X_t$, $X_{t+1}$ and $\Xi_{t+1}\subset\mathbb{R}^q$ are convex, that $\mathbb{P}_{t+1}$ has a finite first
moment, and that, for every $W\in\mathcal{W}^{\rm c}_{t+1}$ and every $y\in X_t$, the map $\xi\mapsto \dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;y,\xi)$ is
convex on $\Xi_{t+1}$ and $L^\xi_t$-Lipschitz. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a finite partition of $\Xi_{t+1}$ into convex Borel cells
$C$, $p_C:=\mathbb{P}_{t+1}(C)$ and, if $p_C>0$, $\xi_C:=\mathbb{E}[\bm{\xi}_{t+1}\mid\bm{\xi}_{t+1}\in C]$. For such a $W$ and $x\in X_t$,
let $f_C$ be an affine $L_t$-Lipschitz minorant of $\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;\cdot,\xi_C)$ on $X_t$ with
$f_C(x)=\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x,\xi_C)$. Then $f:=\sum_{C:\,p_C>0}p_Cf_C$ is affine, $L_t$-Lipschitz, valid for $\mathcal{B}_t(W)$ on $X_t$
and $\gamma$-tight at $x$ with $\gamma\le L^\xi_t\,e(\mathcal{P})$, where
$e(\mathcal{P}):=\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\xi}_{t+1}-\mathbb{E}[\bm{\xi}_{t+1}\mid\mathcal{P}]\|\le\max_{C\in\mathcal{P}}\operatorname{diam} C$. If $\Xi_{t+1}$ lies in a cube $Q$ of side
$D_\infty>0$ and, for $h>0$ and $m:=\lceil D_\infty/h\rceil$, $\mathcal{P}$ consists of the nonempty traces on $\Xi_{t+1}$ of
the $m^q$ boxes obtained by partitioning each side of $Q$ into $m$ intervals of length at most $h$, then
$|\mathcal{P}|\le m^q$ and, for the Euclidean norm, $e(\mathcal{P})\le h\sqrt q/2$.

name: Jensen lower discretisation

title: Proof
body_md:
A probability law carried by a convex set $C$ has its mean in $C$, and Jensen's inequality holds for convex functions
on $C$. Cells with $p_C=0$ do not contribute to $\mathcal{B}_t(W)$; below, sums run over the cells with $p_C>0$, whose
weights add up to one, so $f$ is affine and $L_t$-Lipschitz. For $y\in X_t$,
$\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;y,\xi_C)\le\mathbb{E}[\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;y,\bm{\xi}_{t+1})\mid\bm{\xi}_{t+1}\in C]$, and
$f(y)\le\sum_Cp_C\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;y,\xi_C)\le\mathcal{B}_t(W)(y)$. At $x$,
$\mathcal{B}_t(W)(x)-f(x)=\sum_Cp_C\big(\mathbb{E}[\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x,\bm{\xi}_{t+1})\mid C]-\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x,\xi_C)\big)\le L^\xi_t\sum_Cp_C\mathbb{E}[\|\bm{\xi}_{t+1}-\xi_C\|\mid C]=L^\xi_te(\mathcal{P})$.
For boxes of sides at most $h$, each coordinate of $\bm{\xi}_{t+1}$ lies, given the cell, in an interval of length at
most $h$, so its conditional variance is at most $h^2/4$, and
$e(\mathcal{P})\le(\mathbb{E}\|\bm{\xi}_{t+1}-\mathbb{E}[\bm{\xi}_{t+1}\mid\mathcal{P}]\|^2)^{1/2}\le h\sqrt q/2$.

Let $\|\cdot\|$ be a norm, for which $L_{t+1}$, $L^x_t$ and the diameters are taken. For each $t<T$, let
$\mathcal{W}'_{t+1}$ be the set of $L_{t+1}$-Lipschitz $W$ on $X_{t+1}$ (set $L_T=D_T:=0$, so that the terms of index $T$ vanish) with
$\underline w_{t+1}\le W\le\underline w_{t+1}+B_{t+1}$, and assume that it contains $\mathcal{W}_{t+1}\cup\{V_{t+1}\}$.

$s=t$ and, if $t+1<T$, for $s=t+1$ (see \cref{lem:nets}(a)). Assume that, for all $x,x'\in X_t$,
$\xi\in\Xi_{t+1}$ and $W\in\mathcal{W}'_{t+1}$, $\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x,\cdot)$ takes values in an interval of length $\mathrm{rg}_t$ and

$\mathbb{P}_{t+1}$. Then for every $u>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, for all $t<T$,
\begin{gather}
\sup_{x\in X_t,\,W\in\mathcal{W}'_{t+1}}\big|\mathcal{B}_t(W)(x)-\widehat{\mathcal B}_t(W)(x)\big|
\le4u+\mathrm{rg}_t\sqrt{\frac{\ln\nu_t(u)+\ln(2T/\delta)}{2N}}, \label{eq:appC:uniform_saa_deviation} \\
\ln\nu_t(u):=d\ln\Big(1+\frac{2L^x_tD_t}{u}\Big)+\Big(1+\frac{8L_{t+1}D_{t+1}}{u}\Big)^{d}\ln\Big(1+\frac{2B_{t+1}}{u}\Big). \label{eq:appC:covering_number}
\end{gather}
With $u=N^{-1/(d+2)}$, $\Delta^\pm_t=O\big(N^{-1/(d+2)}\sqrt{\ln N}\big)$, with constants depending on $d$,
$L_{t+1}D_{t+1}$, $L^x_tD_t$, $B_{t+1}$, $\mathrm{rg}_t$ and $\ln(T/\delta)$, but not on $q$.

body_md:
\emph{Nets.} By assumption, take a $(u/L^x_t)$-net $\mathcal N$ of $X_t$ and a $(u/(4L_{t+1}))$-net
$\{z_j\}_{j\in[n_Z]}$ of $X_{t+1}$, with $n_Z\le(1+8L_{t+1}D_{t+1}/u)^d$ (a radius $u/0$ is infinite, and one point
is then a net; this covers $t=T-1$, where $L_T=0$). \emph{Cover of $\mathcal{W}'_{t+1}$.} Code $W$ by the integers
$\lfloor(W(z_j)-\underline w)/(u/2)\rfloor\in\{m\in\mathbb N:m\le\lfloor2B/u\rfloor\}$. If $W,W'$ have the same code,
then for $y\in X_{t+1}$ and $z_j$ with $\|y-z_j\|\le u/(4L_{t+1})$,
$|W(y)-W'(y)|\le|W(y)-W(z_j)|+|W(z_j)-W'(z_j)|+|W'(z_j)-W'(y)|<u$. One member of $\mathcal{W}'_{t+1}$ in each nonempty code
class gives a $u$-cover $\mathcal{W}_u$ in sup norm with $|\mathcal{W}_u|\le(1+2B/u)^{n_Z}$. \emph{Concentration.} For
$(x',W')\in\mathcal N\times\mathcal{W}_u$, $f=\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W';x',\cdot)$ takes values in an interval of length $\mathrm{rg}_t$;
Hoeffding's inequality \citep{hoeffding1963probability} and a union bound over these $\nu_t(u)\ge|\mathcal N||\mathcal{W}_u|$
functions and over $t$ give, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$|\int f\,d(\mathbb{P}_{t+1}-\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{t+1})|\le \mathrm{rg}_t\sqrt{(\ln\nu_t(u)+\ln(2T/\delta))/(2N)}$ for all of them.
\emph{Approximation.} For $(x,W)$, pick $x'\in\mathcal N$ with $\|x-x'\|\le u/L^x_t$ and $W'\in\mathcal{W}_u$ with
$\|W-W'\|_\infty\le u$. Since $\mathcal{X}_{t+1}(x',\xi)\subset X_{t+1}$, $|\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x',\xi)-\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W';x',\xi)|\le u$, so
$|\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x,\xi)-\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W';x',\xi)|\le2u$ for every $\xi\in\Xi_{t+1}$, and both integrals move by at most $2u$. For the
rate, $\ln\nu_t(u)=O(u^{-d}\ln(1/u))$, and $u=N^{-1/(d+2)}$ balances the two terms.

label: rem:bias
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:bias}
In the instance of \cref{prop:counter} (\cref{app:sampled}), with a fixed SAA whose mean exceeds $0.6$, SDDP ends
with a policy that is $0.1$-suboptimal for the true problem, with forward passes from either law; this is consistent
with \cref{thm:saa}, since $\Delta^-_1>0.1$. For the Jensen law $\sum_Cp_C\delta_{\xi_C}$ of \cref{prop:jensen},
$\Delta^-_t\le0$ if $\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(V_{t+1};x,\cdot)$ is convex for every $x\in X_t$ (the lower bound is certified), and
$\Delta^+_t\le L^\xi_te(\mathcal{P})$ if $\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x,\cdot)$ is $L^\xi_t$-Lipschitz for $W\in\mathcal{W}_{t+1}$, as in
\cref{cor:wasserstein}(a). If the forward passes are drawn from $\widehat{\mathbb{P}}$ (classical SDDP on the SAA), \cref{thm:master}
controls the SAA gap; transferring it to the true cost needs regularity of the policy in $\xi$, which greedy argmin
selections do not have in general.
head: environment
name: Bias, and SAA forward passes

label: ass:scen
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:scen}
For every $W\in\mathcal{W}^{\rm c}_{t+1}$ (\cref{app:jensen}), every $x\in X_t$ and every $\xi\in\Xi_{t+1}$, the oracle
returns $a(\xi)=\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;x,\xi)$ and $g(\xi)\in E_t$ with $\|g(\xi)\|\le L_t$ and
$\dot{\mathcal{B}}_t(W;y,\xi)\ge a(\xi)+\langle g(\xi),y-x\rangle$ for all $y\in X_t$, Borel in its inputs, and
$\sup_\xi a(\xi)-\inf_\xi a(\xi)\le \mathrm{rg}_t$.
head: environment
name: Scenario oracle

label: thm:sampled
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:sampled}
Let \cref{ass:S,ass:scen} hold, with a Euclidean norm on $E_t$ in which $D_t\ge\operatorname{diam} X_t$, and assume convex state
sets, convex $L_t$-Lipschitz $\underline V^{0}_{t}$ with $\underline V^{0}_{t}\le\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{0}_{t+1})$, and exact or $\gamma^F$-optimal forward passes from the true laws, with deterministic
$\gamma^{F,k}_t$. Choose $\delta_{k,t}>0$ with $\delta':=\sum_{k\ge1,t<T}\delta_{k,t}\le1$. Let
$b_{k,t}:=b(N_{k,t},\delta_{k,t})$, add the shifted cut $\hat f-b_{k,t}$ at iteration $k$ and index $t$, and set
$\Gamma_k:=2\sum_{t<T}b_{k,t}$; let $\Gamma^F_k$ be the forward-error sum~\eqref{eq:main:error_sums}. There is an
event $A$ with $\mathbb{P}(A)\ge1-\delta'$ on which every cut is valid ($\underline V^{k}_{t}\le V_t$ for all $k,t$), and
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbf 1_A\sum_{k\ge1}\Psi_T((G^k-\Gamma^F_k-\Gamma_k)_+)\big]\le(1+\delta'/2)M^V$, where
$M^V:=\sum_{t<T}\sup_{X_t}(V_t-\underline V^{0}_{t})$;
\item for $\delta\in(0,1]$, with probability at least $1-\delta-\delta'$, simultaneously for all $\theta>0$,
$\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^F_k+\Gamma_k\}\le(9\ln(3/\delta)+\delta'/2)M^V/\Psi_T(\theta)$.
\end{enumerate}
With $\delta_{k,t}=\delta'/(Tk(k+1))$, the condition $\Gamma_k\le g_k$ for a target $g_k>0$ holds as soon as
$N_{k,t}\ge\big(2T(\mathrm{rg}_t+2L_tD_t)/g_k\big)^2\ln\big(4Tk(k+1)/\delta'\big)$.

name: Shifted sampled cuts

label: lem:conc
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:conc}
Let \cref{ass:scen} hold with a Euclidean (Hilbert) norm on $E_t$, and let $\delta\in(0,1]$. For every event
$E\in\mathcal G$ on which $W\in\mathcal{W}^{\rm c}_{t+1}$, almost surely on $E$,
$\mathbb{P}\big(\sup_{y\in X_t}|\hat f(y)-m(y)|>b(N,\delta)\mid\mathcal G\big)\le\delta$.
head: environment
name: Uniform deviation of a sampled affine cut

title: Proof
body_md:
Conditionally on $\mathcal G$ the pairs $(a,g)(\bm{\xi}^k_{t,i})$ are i.i.d.\ with the law obtained by freezing $(x,W)$.
For $y\in X_t$, $\|y-x\|\le D_t$, so $\sup_y|\hat f(y)-m(y)|\le|\bar a-\mathbb{E} a|+D_t\|\bar g-\mathbb{E} g\|$. Hoeffding's
inequality gives $\mathbb{P}(|\bar a-\mathbb{E} a|>\mathrm{rg}_t\sqrt{\ln(4/\delta)/(2N)})\le\delta/2$. The map
$(\xi_i)_i\mapsto\|\bar g-\mathbb{E} g\|$ has bounded differences $2L_t/N$, and $\mathbb{E}\|\bar g-\mathbb{E} g\|\le L_t/\sqrt N$ by the
Hilbert structure, so McDiarmid's inequality gives $\mathbb{P}(\|\bar g-\mathbb{E} g\|>L_t(1+\sqrt{2\ln(2/\delta)})/\sqrt N)\le\delta/2$.
Finally $1+\sqrt{2v}\le2\sqrt{v+\ln2}$ for $v\ge0$, since $4v+4\ln2-(1+\sqrt{2v})^2=(\sqrt{2v}-1)^2+4\ln2-2>0$; with
$v=\ln(2/\delta)$ the sum of the two deviations is at most $b(N,\delta)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Good events.} Let $A_{k,t}:=\{\sup_{X_t}|\hat f-m|\le b_{k,t}\}$, $\Omega_0$ the whole space and
$\Omega_k:=\Omega_{k-1}\cap\bigcap_{t<T}A_{k,t}$, which is $\mathcal{A}_k$-measurable. On $\Omega_{k-1}$, all cuts of
iterations $\le k-1$ are valid, so \cref{lem:valid}(a) gives $\underline V^{j}_{}\le V$ for $j\le k-1$. On
$E:=\Omega_{k-1}\cap\bigcap_{s>t}A_{k,s}\in\mathcal G$, the cuts of indices $s>t$ of iteration $k$ are valid too, so
$W=\underline V^{k}_{t+1}$, the maximum of the convex $\underline V^{0}_{t+1}$ and of valid affine $L_{t+1}$-Lipschitz cuts, lies in
$\mathcal{W}^{\rm c}_{t+1}$. On $E\cap A_{k,t}$, with $b=b_{k,t}$, we have $\hat f-b\le m\le\mathcal{B}_t(W)$ on $X_t$ (validity) and
$(\hat f-b)(x)=\bar a-b\ge\mathcal{B}_t(W)(x)-2b$. By \cref{lem:conc}, the probability that $E$ holds while $A_{k,t}$ fails
is at most $\delta_{k,t}$, also conditionally on $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$. Summing over the first failing index,
$\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{k-1}\setminus \Omega_k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1})\le\sum_{t<T}\delta_{k,t}$. Let $A:=\bigcap_k\Omega_k$; then
$\mathbb{P}(A^c)\le\delta'$.

\emph{Lift on $\Omega_k$.} There, every cut so far is valid and $L_t$-Lipschitz, and the shifted cut at $x$ is at
least $\mathcal{B}_t(\underline V^{k-1}_{t+1})(x)-2b_{k,t}$. As in the proof of \cref{thm:master},
$\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\ge\Psi_T((R^k-\Gamma_k)_+)$. On $\Omega_{k-1}$, $\underline V^{k-1}_{}\le V$, so
$r^k_t\in[0,\sup(V_t-\underline V^{0}_{t})]$ and $R^k\in[0,M^V]$. Also $\Psi_T(u)\le\psi_0(u)\le u/2$
by~\eqref{eq:main:huber_potential}.

\emph{Stopped potential.} Let $\tau_{\rm f}:=\inf\{k:\Omega_k\text{ fails}\}$, a stopping time, and
$Y_k:=\Phi^{k\wedge(\tau_{\rm f}-1)}$. The process $(Y_k)$ is adapted, nondecreasing and bounded by $M^V$, and
$Y_k-Y_{k-1}=\mathbf 1_{\Omega_k}(\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1})$. Using $\Omega_{k-1}\in\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$, conditional Jensen and \cref{lem:gap},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appC:stopped_potential}
\mathbb{E}[Y_k-Y_{k-1}\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]\ge\mathbf 1_{\Omega_{k-1}}\Psi_T\big((G^k-\Gamma^F_k-\Gamma_k)_+\big)-\tfrac{M^V}2\,\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{k-1}\setminus \Omega_k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}).
\end{equation}
Summing and taking expectations gives~(i), since $\mathbb{E}\lim_kY_k\le M^V$,
$\sum_k\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{k-1}\setminus \Omega_k)\le\delta'$ and $\mathbf 1_A\le\mathbf 1_{\Omega_{k-1}}$. For~(ii), apply \cref{lem:dbp}
to $M^V-Y_k$: with probability at least $1-\delta$ its regret is at most $9M^V\ln(3/\delta)$, and
by~\eqref{eq:appC:stopped_potential} it is at least
$\sum_{k\ge1}\mathbf 1_{\Omega_{k-1}}\Psi_T((G^k-\Gamma^F_k-\Gamma_k)_+)-M^V\delta'/2$; intersect with $A$. Finally,
$2\sum_{t<T}b_{k,t}\le g_k$ if each $b_{k,t}\le g_k/(2T)$; solving for $N$ gives the sample-size condition.

label: prop:counter
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:counter}
Let $T=2$, $X_0=\{x_0\}$, $\mathcal{X}_1(x_0,\xi)=[0,1]$, $\ell_1\equiv0$, $X_1=[0,1]$, $\mathcal{X}_2(x,\xi)=\{0\}$,
$\ell_2(x,0,\xi)=\xi x+0.6(1-x)$ with $\bm{\xi}_2\sim U[0,1]$, and $\underline V^{0}_{}\equiv0$. Then $V_1(x)=0.6-0.1x$ and
$V_0(x_0)=0.5$, attained only at $x_1=1$. Run SDDP with exact forward passes and raw sampled cuts at index~1, built
from fresh samples of sizes $N_k\ge1$. If the cut of iteration $j$ is built from a sample with mean $\bar\xi_j>0.6$, then at every
iteration $k>j$ the policy plays $x_1=0$, $V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)=0.6=V_0(x_0)+0.1$ and $\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)=0.6>V_0(x_0)$; in
particular $G^k=0$ although $\pi^k$ is $0.1$-suboptimal. This happens with probability at least
$\mathbb{P}(\bar\xi_1>0.6)>0$ for every choice of sample sizes, and almost surely if $\sup_kN_k<\infty$.
head: environment
name: Raw sampled cuts can stall SDDP

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $\xi$, $y\mapsto \dot{\mathcal{B}}_1(0;y,\xi)=\xi y+0.6(1-y)$ is affine, so its exact scenario cut is itself, and a raw
sampled cut is the line $f_j(y)=\bar\xi_jy+0.6(1-y)$, through $(0,0.6)$ and $(1,\bar\xi_j)$. Hence $\underline V^{k}_{1}(0)=0.6$ for
$k\ge1$. If $\bar\xi_j>0.6$ for some $j\le k-1$, then $\underline V^{k-1}_{1}(y)\ge0.6+(\bar\xi_j-0.6)y>0.6$ for $y\in(0,1]$, so the
forward pass of iteration $k$ plays $x_1=0$. Index~0 is deterministic with $d_0=0$; its exact cut gives
$\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)=\min_{[0,1]}\underline V^{k-1}_{1}=0.6$, while $V^{\pi^k}_0(x_0)=V_1(0)=0.6$. Cuts are never removed, so this
persists. The mean of $N$ i.i.d.\ $U[0,1]$ variables has a positive density on $(0,1)$, so $\mathbb{P}(\bar\xi>0.6)>0$. The
cuts use independent samples, so if $N_k\le\bar N$ for all $k$, an exceedance occurs almost surely.

label: prop:unbounded
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:unbounded}
Let $X'_t\supset X_t$ be Borel sets with $\emptyset\ne \mathcal{X}_t(x,\xi)\subset X'_t$ for $x\in X'_{t-1}$, $\xi\in\Xi_t$,
where the $X_t$ are convex and compact with normalised Lebesgue measure. Let \cref{ass:S} hold with $X'_t$ in place
of $X_t$, except that compactness is dropped and the uniform bound in~\ref{S2} is replaced by integrability of
$\ell_t$, $V_t$ and $\underline V^{0}_{t}$ along the forward paths. Assume that $\underline V^{0}_{t}\le V_t$ on $X'_t$ and that $\underline V^{0}_{t}$ is
$L_t$-Lipschitz on $X_t$, that the cuts are valid on $X'_t$ (below $V_t$), $L_t$-Lipschitz on $X_t$ and $\gamma$-tight
as in \cref{sec:route2}, and that for all $k$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appC:outside_residual}
\Delta^{\rm out}_k:=\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{t<T}r^k_t(\bm{x}^k_t)\,\mathbf 1\{\bm{x}^k_t\notin X_t\}\ \Big|\ \mathcal{A}_{k-1}\Big]\le\Delta^{\rm out} .
\end{equation}
Then $\mathbb{E}\big[\sum_{k\ge1}\Psi_T((G^k-\bar{\bm{\Gamma}}_k-\Delta^{\rm out})_+)\big]\le M^V:=\sum_{t<T}\sup_{X_t}(V_t-\underline V^{0}_{t})$.
The bound on $\Delta^{\rm out}_k$ holds in either of two cases: $r^k_t\le M'_t$ on $X'_t$ for some $M'_t\ge0$ and
$\mathbb{P}(\bm{x}^k_t\notin X_t\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1})\le o_t$, with $\Delta^{\rm out}=\sum_tM'_to_t$; or
$\mathbb{E}[(V_t-\underline V^{0}_{t})(\bm{x}^k_t)^2\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]\le\bar m_t^2$ and the same $o_t$, with $\Delta^{\rm out}=\sum_t\bar m_t\sqrt{o_t}$.

name: Leaving the compact set

title: Proof
body_md:
Validity on $X'_t$ and $\underline V^{0}_{t}\le V_t$ give $\underline V^{0}_{t}\le\underline V^{k}_{t}\le V_t$ on $X'_t$. Since $\mathcal{X}_{t+1}(x,\xi)\subset X'_{t+1}$
for $x\in X'_t$ and $\mathcal{B}_t$ is monotone, $r^k_t\le\mathcal{B}_t(V_{t+1})-\underline V^{0}_{t}=V_t-\underline V^{0}_{t}$ there (residuals may be negative).
\Cref{lem:gap} holds with $X'_t$ in place of $X_t$, by the same telescoping: $\underline V^{k-1}_{t}(\bm{x}^k_t)$ is integrable because
$\underline V^{0}_{t}\le\underline V^{k-1}_{t}\le V_t$, and so is every $r^k_t(\bm{x}^k_t)$, by the one-step
identity~\eqref{eq:main:one_step_expectation}. The potential is computed on the compact sets $X_t$, where it is at
most $M^V$, and \cref{lem:lift} is applied only at trial points in $X_t$. Let
$\tilde R^k:=\sum_{t<T}r^k_t(\bm{x}^k_t)\mathbf 1\{\bm{x}^k_t\in X_t\}$, which is integrable and at most $M^V$. Since
$\sum_{t<T}(r^k_t(\bm{x}^k_t)-\bm{\gamma}^k_t)_+\mathbf 1\{\bm{x}^k_t\in X_t\}\ge(\tilde R^k-\bm{\Gamma}_k)_+$, we get
$\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\ge\Psi_T((\tilde R^k-\bm{\Gamma}_k)_+)$. Then
$\mathbb{E}[\tilde R^k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]=\mathbb{E}[R^k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]-\Delta^{\rm out}_k\ge G^k-\Gamma^F_k-\Delta^{\rm out}$; conclude as
in \cref{thm:master}. For the second sufficient condition, use Cauchy--Schwarz and $r^k_t\le V_t-\underline V^{0}_{t}$.

head: environment
name: Standard facts

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) Since $\emptyset\ne\mathcal{X}(x,\xi)\subset X$ and $\ell\in[0,\bar\ell]$, $\beta\inf W\le\dot{\mathcal{B}}(W;x,\xi)\le\bar\ell+\beta\sup W$, and
Fubini's theorem makes $\mathcal{B} W$ Borel; monotonicity and the shift are immediate, and give the contraction. If
$W_j\to W$ uniformly, $|\dot{\mathcal{B}}(W_j;x,\xi)-\dot{\mathcal{B}}(W;x,\xi)|\le\beta\sup|W_j-W|$, so $\dot{\mathcal{B}}(W;\cdot,\cdot)$ is a pointwise limit of
jointly measurable functions. (ii) $V=\mathcal{B} V\ge\beta\inf V$ gives $\inf V\ge0$, and $V\le\bar\ell+\beta\sup V$ gives $\sup V\le\bar\ell/(1-\beta)$.
If $W\le\mathcal{B} W$ and $c:=\sup(W-V)_+$, then $W\le V+c$ and $W\le\mathcal{B} W\le\mathcal{B}(V+c)=V+\beta c$, so $c\le\beta c$ and
$c=0$. Uniqueness and convergence follow from the contraction. (iii) Let $\lambda_t:=\ell(\bm{x}_t,\bm{x}_{t+1},\bm{\xi}_{t+1})$ and
$\mathcal H_t$ the $\sigma$-field of the conditioning and of $\bm{\xi}_{[t]}$. As $\lambda_t+\beta V(\bm{x}_{t+1})\ge\dot{\mathcal{B}}(V;\bm{x}_t,\bm{\xi}_{t+1})$,
the freezing property gives $\mathbb{E}[\lambda_t+\beta V(\bm{x}_{t+1})\mid\mathcal H_t]\ge V(\bm{x}_t)$. Iterate from $t=1$ and let the
horizon tend to infinity ($V$ is bounded): $V^\pi(x_0)\ge\mathbb{E}[\lambda_0+\beta V(\bm{x}_1)]$, and $t=0$ gives $\ge V(x_0)$.

label: lem:validIH
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:validIH}
Assume \cref{ass:Sinf}, and let every cut be computed for the current model $W$. (a) If $\underline V^{0}\le V$ and every cut
satisfies $f\le\mathcal{B} W$ on $X$, then every model is $\le V$, so~\ref{OI3} holds with $U=V$ and $M_U\le\bar\ell/(1-\beta)-\inf_X\underline V^{0}$. If moreover
$\underline V^{0}\le\mathcal{B}\underline V^{0}$ (e.g.\ $\underline V^{0}=0$), the assumption $\underline V^{0}\le V$ holds by \cref{lem:std}(ii), and every model satisfies
$W\le\mathcal{B} W$, so $r^k\ge0$. (b) Under~\ref{OI4}, if
$f(x)\ge\mathcal{B} W(x)-\gamma_{k,t}$ at $x=\bm{x}^k_t$, then~\ref{OI2} holds.
head: environment
name: Sufficient conditions

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) If $\underline V^{0}\le\mathcal{B}\underline V^{0}$, then $\underline V^{0}\le V$ by \cref{lem:std}(ii). By induction on the cuts, let $W\le V$ be the current
model and $f$ a cut; then $f\le\mathcal{B} W\le\mathcal{B} V=V$, so $\max(W,f)\le V$. If moreover $W\le\mathcal{B} W$, then, with
$W':=\max(W,f)\ge W$, $W\le\mathcal{B} W\le\mathcal{B} W'$ and $f\le\mathcal{B} W\le\mathcal{B} W'$, so $W'\le\mathcal{B} W'$. (b) By~\ref{OI4},
$W\ge\underline V^{k-1}$, and $\mathcal{B}$ is monotone.

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\underline V^{}:=\underline V^{k-1}$, $r_t:=r^k(\bm{x}_t)$ and $\mathcal H_t:=\mathcal{A}_{k-1}\vee\sigma(\bm{\xi}_{[t]})$. The bounds on $e_t$ are the
definitions of $\pi^k$ and $\dot{\mathcal{B}}$. By the freezing property and~\ref{SI3},

label: lem:length
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:length}
Let $(r_t)_{t\ge0}\subset[0,R]$, $\bar r_0:=0$, $\bar r_n:=\max_{t<n}r_t$ ($n\ge1$), and $\tau$ a random variable in
$\mathbb N^*$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $\mathbb{E}\,\bar r_\tau=\sum_{s\ge0}\mathbb{P}(\tau>s)\,(\bar r_{s+1}-\bar r_s)$.
\item If $\mathbb{P}(\tau>s)\ge\beta^s$ for all $s\ge0$, then
$\mathbb{E}\,\bar r_\tau\ge(1-\beta)\sum_{n\ge1}\beta^{n-1}\bar r_n\ge(1-\beta)\sum_{t\ge0}\beta^tr_t$. Conversely, if $R>0$ and
$\mathbb{E}\,\bar r_\tau\ge(1-\beta)\sum_t\beta^tr_t$ for every such sequence, then $\mathbb{P}(\tau>s)\ge\beta^s$ for all $s$.
Under this condition $\mathbb{E}\tau\ge1/(1-\beta)$, with equality iff $\mathbb{P}(\tau>s)=\beta^s$ for all $s$.
\item For a deterministic $\tau=H$:
$\bar r_H\ge\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^H}\sum_{t<H}\beta^tr_t\ge(1-\beta)\sum_{t<H}\beta^tr_t$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Pass lengths

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) Write $\bar r_n=\sum_{s<n}(\bar r_{s+1}-\bar r_s)$ and use Tonelli; the increments are nonnegative.
(ii) Hence $\mathbb{E}\bar r_\tau\ge\sum_s\beta^s(\bar r_{s+1}-\bar r_s)=(1-\beta)\sum_{n\ge1}\beta^{n-1}\bar r_n$ (the
series converge since $\bar r$ is bounded); then use $\bar r_n\ge r_{n-1}$. For the converse, take
$r_t=R\mathbf 1\{t\ge s\}$: then $\bar r_n=R\mathbf 1\{n>s\}$, $\mathbb{E}\bar r_\tau=R\,\mathbb{P}(\tau>s)$ and
$(1-\beta)\sum_{t\ge s}\beta^tR=R\beta^s$. Finally $\mathbb{E}\tau=\sum_s\mathbb{P}(\tau>s)\ge\sum_s\beta^s$.
(iii) $\sum_{t<H}\beta^tr_t\le\bar r_H(1-\beta^H)/(1-\beta)$.

label: lem:length-phase
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:length-phase}
Let $(r_t)_{t\ge0}\subset[0,R]$, let $\tau\in\mathbb N^*$ satisfy $\mathbb{P}(\tau>s)=\beta^s$ for all $s\ge0$, and, for
$p\in\mathbb Z_S$, let $\bar r_{(p)}:=\max\{r_t:t<\tau,\ p(t)=p\}$, with $\max\emptyset:=0$. Then
$\mathbb{E}\,\bar r_{(p)}\ge(1-\beta^S)\sum_{t\ge0:\,p(t)=p}\beta^tr_t$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $q_j:=r_{p+jS}$ for $j\ge0$, $\bar q_0:=0$, $\bar q_n:=\max_{j<n}q_j$ for $n\ge1$, and $N:=\#\{j\ge0:p+jS<\tau\}$, so
that $\bar r_{(p)}=\bar q_N$ and $\mathbb{P}(N>j)=\beta^{p+jS}$. The identity of \cref{lem:length}(i) holds for every random
variable with values in $\mathbb N$, so $\mathbb{E}\,\bar r_{(p)}=\sum_{j\ge0}\beta^{p+jS}(\bar q_{j+1}-\bar q_j)
=\beta^p(1-\beta^S)\sum_{n\ge1}\beta^{S(n-1)}\bar q_n\ge\beta^p(1-\beta^S)\sum_{j\ge0}\beta^{jS}q_j$, since $\bar q$ is
bounded and $\bar q_n\ge q_{n-1}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $k\ge1$, couple the pass with an infinite trajectory $(\bm{x}_t)_{t\ge0}$ of $\pi^k$ from $x_0$, independent of
$\tau_k$ given $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$, and let $r_t:=r^k_{p(t)}(\bm{x}_t)$ and $s_t:=(r_t-\gamma_{k,t})_+$. On the
$\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$-measurable event where $\sum_t\beta^t\gamma_{k,t}=\infty$, $\Gamma^\beta_k=\infty$ and there is nothing to
prove, since $\Phi^k\ge\Phi^{k-1}$; we work on its complement. Models, residuals and $s_t$ are bounded (\cref{lem:pass}).

\emph{Gap identity.} (i) is \cref{lem:gapIH} with $\tau=\tau_k$, with~\eqref{eq:inf:gap_meaning}, which follows from
\cref{lem:std}(iii) and $\underline V^{k-1}_0(x_0)\le\bar U_0(x_0)\le U_0(x_0)$. By \cref{lem:gapIH} with $H=0$ and $e_t\le\gamma^F_k$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appD:inexact_gap}
\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\sum_{t\ge0}\beta^t(r_t-\gamma_{k,t})\ \ge\ G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k .
\end{equation}

\emph{Pathwise lift.} As in the proof of \cref{lem:pass}, at $t<\tau_k$, with $x:=\bm{x}^k_t$ and $p:=p(t)$,
$\underline V^{k}_p(x)\ge\underline V^{k-1}_p(x)+s_t$ and $\underline V^{k}_p\ge\underline V^{k-1}_p$, so
$\int(\underline V^{k}_p-\underline V^{k-1}_p)\,d\mu_p\ge\kappa\hat\psi(\bar s_p)$ with $\bar s_p:=\max\{s_t:t<\tau_k,\ p(t)=p\}$ ($\max\emptyset:=0$).
Summing over $p$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appD:periodic_pathwise}
\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\ \ge\ \Lambda_k:=\kappa\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z_S}\hat\psi(\bar s_p),
\end{equation}
which is~\eqref{eq:inf:periodic_lift}, and implies \cref{lem:pass} ($S=1$).

\emph{Lower bounds.} First, $\Lambda_k\ge\kappa\hat\psi(\bar s)$ with $\bar s:=\max_{t<\tau_k}s_t=\max_p\bar s_p$. Given
$\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$ and the path, \cref{lem:length}(ii) gives $\mathbb{E}[\bar s\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1},\text{path}]\ge(1-\beta)\sum_t\beta^ts_t$, so
$\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\bar s\ge(1-\beta)(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+$ by $s_t\ge\max\{0,r_t-\gamma_{k,t}\}$ and~\eqref{eq:appD:inexact_gap}, and
conditional Jensen ($\hat\psi$ is convex and $\bar s$ is bounded) gives
$\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\Lambda_k\ge\kappa\hat\psi\big((1-\beta)(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+\big)$. Second, by \cref{lem:length-phase},
$a_p:=\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\bar s_p\ge0$ satisfies $\sum_pa_p\ge(1-\beta^S)\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\sum_t\beta^ts_t\ge(1-\beta^S)(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+$,
and conditional Jensen, convexity and monotonicity of $\hat\psi$ give
$\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\Lambda_k\ge\kappa\sum_p\hat\psi(a_p)\ge\kappa S\hat\psi\big(\sum_pa_p/S\big)\ge\kappa S\hat\psi\big((1-\beta^S)(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+/S\big)$.
Hence $\mathbb{E}_{k-1}[\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}]\ge\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\Lambda_k\ge\kappa\chi_S((G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+)$.

\emph{Summation and rates.} Sum over $k$, with $0=\Phi^0\le\Phi^k\le\bar M_U$. On $\{G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta\}$ the $k$-th
term is at least $\kappa\chi_S(\theta)$, as $\chi_S$ is nondecreasing. If
$(1-\beta)\theta\le\hat\rho$, then $(1-\beta^S)\theta/S=(1-\beta)\theta/q_S\le\hat\rho$ too, both evaluations of
$\hat\psi$ are on its first branch, and $\chi_S(\theta)=\max\{1,S/q_S^{d+1}\}((1-\beta)\theta)^{d+1}/(2(d+1)\hat\rho^d)$.
For~(iii), apply \cref{lem:dbp} with $Y_k:=\bar M_U-\Phi^k$ ($Y_0=\bar M_U$ is deterministic) and
$f_k:=\kappa\chi_S((G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+)$, which is $\mathcal{A}_{k-1}$-measurable. For $S=1$, $q_S=1$ and these are the
statements of \cref{thm:master-ih}(a); the cut count follows from $\mathbb{E}[\tau_k\mid\mathcal{A}_{k-1}]=1/(1-\beta)$. For SDDP,
$\bar M_U\le S\bar\ell/(1-\beta)$ and $q_S\le\min\{S,1+S(1-\beta)\}$ give the bound stated after \cref{thm:periodic}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Y_k:=\sum_{c\in C}(\bar U-\underline V^{k})(c)$; by the bounds after \cref{ass:Oinf}, $(Y_k)$ is adapted, nonincreasing and
nonnegative, and $Y_0=M_C$ is deterministic. Fix $k\ge1$ and $t<\tau_k$, let $x:=\bm{x}^k_t$, and choose $c\in C$ with
$\operatorname{dist}(x,c)\le\sigma$. As in the proof of \cref{lem:pass}, $(\underline V^{k}-\underline V^{k-1})(x)\ge s^k_t$; both models are
$\hat L$-Lipschitz, so $(\underline V^{k}-\underline V^{k-1})(c)\ge(s^k_t-2\hat L\sigma)_+$, and the other lifts are nonnegative. Different $t$
may give the same $c$, so only the maximum is available: $Y_{k-1}-Y_k\ge(\bar s^k-2\hat L\sigma)_+$. By conditional Jensen for $(\cdot)_+$, then
$\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\bar s^k\ge(1-\beta)(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+$ (proof of \cref{thm:periodic}) and $2\hat L\sigma\le(1-\beta)\theta/2$,
\[
\mathbb{E}_{k-1}[Y_{k-1}-Y_k]\ \ge\ \big(\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\bar s^k-2\hat L\sigma\big)_+\ \ge\ (1-\beta)\big(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k-\theta/2\big)_+=:f_k .
\]
Sum over $k\in[K]$ and let $K\to\infty$: $\mathbb{E}\sum_kf_k\le Y_0=M_C$. The count follows from
$(\theta/2)\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta_k\}\le\sum_{k\ge1}(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k-\theta/2)_+$, and the high-probability
claim is \cref{lem:dbp} applied to $(Y_k)$, with $C=M_C$ and these $f_k$. The net size is \cref{lem:nets}(a) with
$2D/\sigma=8\hat L D/((1-\beta)\theta)$. For~(c), $\bar U=U$ because $\operatorname{dist}=+\infty$ off the diagonal; take $C=X$, $c=x$,
$\sigma=0$ and $\theta=0$, so that the Lipschitz property is not used, with $f_k=(1-\beta)(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+$ and
$Y_0=C_{\rm fin}$. For periodic problems, take one net $C_p$ per phase, $Y_k:=\sum_p\sum_{c\in C_p}(\bar U_p-\underline V^{k}_p)(c)$
and $c\in C_{p(t)}$; the argument is unchanged.

name: Deterministic pass length

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) Let $s_t:=s^k_t$ and $r_t:=r^k(\bm{x}^k_t)$. By \cref{lem:pass} and \cref{lem:length}(iii),
$\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}\ge\kappa\hat\psi\big((1-\beta)\sum_{t<H}\beta^ts_t\big)$. By \cref{lem:gapIH},
$\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\sum_{t<H}\beta^t(r_t-\gamma_{k,t})\ge G^k-\varepsilon^k_H-\Gamma^\beta_k$, and $\varepsilon^k_H\le\varepsilon_H$
as $\underline V^{k-1}\ge\underline V^{0}\ge0$; since $s_t\ge\max\{0,r_t-\gamma_{k,t}\}$, $\mathbb{E}_{k-1}\sum_{t<H}\beta^ts_t\ge(G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k-\varepsilon_H)_+$.
Conditional Jensen gives the first claim; sum over $k$, with $0=\Phi^0\le\Phi^k\le\bar M_U$. On $\{G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta\}$, $(G^k-\Gamma^\beta-\varepsilon_H)_+\ge(1-\varsigma)\theta$, so the $k$-th term is at
least $\kappa\hat\psi((1-\varsigma)(1-\beta)\theta)=\kappa((1-\varsigma)(1-\beta)\theta)^{d+1}/(2(d+1)\hat\rho^d)$ (first branch).
For the high-probability bound, apply \cref{lem:dbp} with $Y_k:=\bar M_U-\Phi^k$; its regret is at least
$\kappa\hat\psi((1-\varsigma)(1-\beta)\theta)\,\#\{k\in[K]:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta_k\}$, and the exceptional event does not depend on
$\theta$. (ii) $\beta^H\le e^{-(1-\beta)H}\le(1-\beta)\theta/((d+2)\bar\ell)$, so $\varepsilon_H\le\theta/(d+2)$; take
$\varsigma=1/(d+2)$, which costs only $\ln(d+2)/(1-\beta)$ more steps per pass than $\varsigma=1/2$, and use $(1+1/(d+1))^{d+1}\le e$. The first index with $G^k\le\theta+\Gamma^\beta$ is at most
$1+\#\{k\ge1:G^k>\theta+\Gamma^\beta\}$.

label: prop:ih-saa
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ih-saa}
Let $\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_p$ be laws on $\Xi_p$, fixed or drawn independently of the forward noises and of the pass lengths, with
periodic operators $\widehat{\mathcal B}_p$ as in \cref{sec:periodic} and fixed point $\widehat V$. Assume \cref{ass:Sinf} phase by
phase for both laws, $\gamma^F$-greedy forward passes from the true laws, $\underline V^{0}_p$ and all cuts $\hat L$-Lipschitz for a norm,
$\underline V^{0}_p\le\widehat V_p$, and cuts exact for $\widehat{\mathcal B}$ and the current models $W$ ($f\le\widehat{\mathcal B}_pW_{p+1}$ on
$X_p$, with equality at the trial point). With $\mathcal{W}_p$ the set
of $\hat L$-Lipschitz $W:X_p\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\underline V^{0}_p\le W\le\widehat V_p$, let, as in the SAA biases~\eqref{eq:noise:saa_biases},
$\Delta^+:=\max_p\sup\{(\mathcal{B}_pW-\widehat{\mathcal B}_pW)(x):x\in X_p,\ W\in\mathcal{W}_{p+1}\}$ and
$\Delta^-:=\max_p\sup_{X_p}(\widehat{\mathcal B}_pV_{p+1}-\mathcal{B}_pV_{p+1})$. Then, conditionally on $\widehat{\mathbb{P}}$ (all statements hold under $\mathbb{P}(\cdot\mid\widehat{\mathbb{P}})$), \cref{ass:Oinf} holds
with $U=\widehat V$ and $\gamma_{k,t}=(\Delta^+)_+$, so \cref{thm:periodic} applies under~\eqref{eq:setting:volume_growth}, with
$\Gamma^\beta_k=((\Delta^+)_++\gamma^F)/(1-\beta)$ and $\bar M_U\le\sum_p\int(\widehat V_p-\underline V^{0}_p)\,d\mu_p$, and
$\zeta\le(\Delta^-)_+/(1-\beta)$. If the maps $\xi\mapsto\inf_{y\in\mathcal{X}_p(x,\xi)}[\ell_p(x,y,\xi)+\beta W(y)]$, for
$x\in X_p$ and $W\in\mathcal{W}_{p+1}\cup\{V_{p+1}\}$, are $L^\xi$-Lipschitz on $\Xi_p$, then $\Delta^\pm\le L^\xi\max_p\mathsf W_1(\mathbb{P}_p,\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_p)$.

name: SAA backward passes, true-law forward passes

title: Proof
body_md:
As for \cref{thm:saa}, apply \cref{lem:validIH}(a) (periodic) to the problem with laws $\widehat{\mathbb{P}}$: since $\underline V^{0}\le\widehat V$ and every cut satisfies
$f\le\widehat{\mathcal B}_pW_{p+1}$, every model satisfies $W_p\le\widehat V_p$, so~\ref{OI3} holds with the ceiling $U=\widehat V$, and every model
of phase $p$ lies in $\mathcal{W}_p$ by~\ref{OI1}. At $x=\bm{x}^k_t$, the current models satisfy $W\ge\underline V^{k-1}$, so
$f(x)=\widehat{\mathcal B}_pW_{p+1}(x)\ge\widehat{\mathcal B}_p\underline V^{k-1}_{p+1}(x)\ge\mathcal{B}_p\underline V^{k-1}_{p+1}(x)-\Delta^+$, because $\underline V^{k-1}_{p+1}\in\mathcal{W}_{p+1}$:
this is~\ref{OI2} with the deterministic error $(\Delta^+)_+$. Also $\bar U_p\le\widehat V_p$.
For $\zeta$, let $e:=\max_p\sup_{X_p}(\widehat V_p-V_p)_+$. Since $\widehat{\mathcal B}_p$ is monotone and
$\widehat{\mathcal B}_p(W+c)=\widehat{\mathcal B}_pW+\beta c$ for constants $c$,
$\widehat V_p-V_p=(\widehat{\mathcal B}_p\widehat V_{p+1}-\widehat{\mathcal B}_pV_{p+1})+(\widehat{\mathcal B}_pV_{p+1}-\mathcal{B}_pV_{p+1})\le\beta e+\Delta^-$, so
$e\le\beta e+(\Delta^-)_+$, that is, $\zeta\le e\le(\Delta^-)_+/(1-\beta)$. For the Wasserstein bound, $(\mathcal{B}_pW-\widehat{\mathcal B}_pW)(x)$
is the integral of an $L^\xi$-Lipschitz function against $\mathbb{P}_p-\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_p$; use Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality.

body_md:
\label{prop:ih-sampled}
Assume \cref{ass:I} phase by phase for general laws, without~\ref{I3}, with $\gamma^F$-greedy forward
passes from the true laws. At $\bm{x}^k_t$, add the shifted sampled cut of \cref{app:sampled} for $\mathcal{B}_{p(t)}$ and the
current models, built from a deterministic number $N_{k,t}$ of fresh i.i.d.\ draws from $\mathbb{P}_{p(t)}$ and the scenario oracle of \cref{ass:scen}
(values and subgradients of norm at most $\hat L$ of $\inf_y[\ell_p(\cdot,y,\xi)+\beta W(y)]$ for every convex
$\hat L$-Lipschitz $W$ with $\underline V^{0}_{p+1}\le W\le V_{p+1}$, with range at most
$\mathrm{rg}$ in $\xi$, for instance $\mathrm{rg}\le\bar\ell+\hat L D$), with
the shift $b_{k,t}:=(\mathrm{rg}+2\hat L D)\sqrt{\ln(4/\delta_{k,t})/N_{k,t}}$, $\delta_{k,t}:=\delta'/(k(k+1)(t+1)(t+2))$ and
$\delta'\in(0,1]$. Let $\Gamma^\beta_k:=2\sum_{t\ge0}\beta^tb_{k,t}+\gamma^F/(1-\beta)$ and
$M^V:=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z_S}\sup_{X_p}(V_p-\underline V^{0}_p)$. There is an event $A$ with $\mathbb{P}(A)\ge1-\delta'$ on which every cut is
valid, and $\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbf 1_A\sum_{k\ge1}\chi_S((G^k-\Gamma^\beta_k)_+)\big]\le(1+\delta'/2)\,M^V$. If
$N_{k,t}\ge\big(2(\mathrm{rg}+2\hat L D)/((1-\beta)g)\big)^2\ln\big(4k(k+1)(t+1)(t+2)/\delta'\big)$ for all $t$, then
$\Gamma^\beta_k\le g+\gamma^F/(1-\beta)$. For $g=\varepsilon_{\rm rel}\bar\ell/(1-\beta)$ and $\mathrm{rg}\le\bar\ell+\hat L D$, this sample size suffices:
$\big(2(1+3\hat L D/\bar\ell)/\varepsilon_{\rm rel}\big)^2\ln\big(4k(k+1)(t+1)(t+2)/\delta'\big)$; for a $\beta$-uniform $\hat L$, it is independent of $\beta$ except through the
logarithm, and of the noise dimension.

title: Proof
body_md:
We follow the proof of \cref{thm:sampled}, with $A_{k,t}:=\{\sup_{X_{p(t)}}|\hat f-m|\le b_{k,t}\}$ for the cut at $\bm{x}^k_t$,

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),nosep]

(losses $\ell^R$), $\hat L=\sum_\xi\mathbb{P}(\xi)(l_{\xi,\lambda}+l_{\xi,\varrho})$, $\gamma_{k,t}=0$ and $U=V$, so
$\zeta=V(x_0)-V^R(x_0)$, or, under \cref{lem:ZSreg}, $U=V^R$ and $\zeta=0$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) $X$ and the noise are finite, so~\ref{SI3} is not needed, every function on $X$ is $0$-Lipschitz for this metric,
and $\bar U=U$. Validity on $X$ and tightness at binary trial points are properties of one nodal problem, here with
$\beta W$, a maximum of affine functions, as cost-to-go term: \citet[Thm.~3]{zou2019sddip} for Lagrangian cuts with
optimal multipliers, and their~(4.2) for integer optimality cuts. So \cref{lem:validIH} gives~\ref{OI2} with
$\gamma_{k,t}=0$ and~\ref{OI3} with $U=V$, and $C_{\rm fin}=\sum_xV(x)\le|X|\bar\ell/(1-\beta)$. (b) $f$ is continuous and
$\hat L$-Lipschitz, and $f(x)=\mathcal{B} W(x)$, so~\ref{OI2} holds by \cref{lem:validIH}(b). By induction, if $W\le V$, then
$f(y)\le\mathcal{B} V(x)-\hat L\|y-x\|=V(x)-\hat L\|y-x\|\le V(y)$, so every model is $\le V$. \emph{Stage-wise absorption.} If
$\mathcal{X}(\cdot,\xi)$ is constant on $X$ and $\ell(\cdot,y,\xi)$ is $c$-Lipschitz for $\operatorname{dist}$, comparing the infima over the
common set gives $\dot{\mathcal{B}}(W;x,\xi)-\dot{\mathcal{B}}(W;x',\xi)\le c\operatorname{dist}(x,x')$ for $W\in\mathfrak M$, so $\mathcal{B} W$ and $V=\mathcal{B} V$ are
$c$-Lipschitz, uniformly in $\beta$, and~(b) applies with $\hat L=c$ and $\underline V^{0}=0$. (c) With
$\ell^R(\bar x,y,\xi):=\inf\{\ell(z,y,\xi)+\varpi_\xi\mathcal R_\xi(\bar x-z):z\in X,\ y\in\mathcal{X}(z,\xi)\}$ and
$\mathcal{X}^R(\bar x,\xi):=\bigcup_{z\in X}\mathcal{X}(z,\xi)\subset X$, $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm R}$ is the operator~\eqref{eq:inf:bellman_operator} of the
regularised problem (\cref{app:ZS}), and $0\le\ell^R\le\bar\ell+\varpi_\xi\sup_{X-X}\mathcal R_\xi$. The checks
of~\ref{O1}--\ref{O4} in the proofs of \cref{prop:ZS,lem:ZSreg} concern one nodal problem; with $\beta W$ as cost-to-go
term, they give $\hat L$-Lipschitz averaged cuts $f\le\mathcal{B} W$ (and $f\le\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm R} W$ under the conditions of \cref{lem:ZSreg}) with
$f(\bar x)\ge\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm R} W(\bar x)$. So~\ref{OI1} holds, and \cref{lem:validIH}, for $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm R}$ for~\ref{OI2} and for $\mathcal{B}$ (respectively
$\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm R}$) for~\ref{OI3}, gives the rest. Finally $z=\bar x$ is feasible, so $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm R} W\le\mathcal{B} W$, and $V^R=\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm R} V^R\le\mathcal{B} V^R$
gives $V^R\le V$ by \cref{lem:std}(ii).

name: Slopes of a cut

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Lipschitz constant.} Write $f=f(x)+\langle g,\cdot-x\rangle$, and let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection
onto the direction space of $\operatorname{aff} X$. If $\Pi g\ne0$, the point $z:=x+\eta\,\Pi g/\|\Pi g\|$ lies in $X_\eta$, so
$\mathcal{B} W(x)+\eta\|\Pi g\|=f(z)\le\mathcal{B} W(z)$, that is, $\|\Pi g\|\le\Theta/\eta$. For $y,y'\in\operatorname{aff} X$,
$|f(y)-f(y')|=|\langle\Pi g,y-y'\rangle|$. \emph{Lower bound at $x$.} Losses are nonnegative and
$\mathcal{X}(x,\xi)\subset X$, so $\mathcal{B} W(x)\ge\beta\inf_X W$. (i) For $z\inX_\eta$, $\mathcal{X}(z,\xi)\subset X$, so
$\mathcal{B} W(z)\le\bar\ell+\beta\sup_X W$. (ii) For $z\inX_\eta$, $\mathcal{X}(z,\xi)=X$, so $\mathcal{B} W(z)\le\bar\ell+\beta\inf_X W$.
(iii) Fix $z\inX_\eta$, $\epsilon_0>0$ and $y\in X$ with $W(y)\le\inf_X W+\epsilon_0$. Take the policy and the stopping
time of $(R_{m,\chi})$, write $\ell_s:=\ell(\bm{x}_s,\bm{x}_{s+1},\bm{\xi}_{s+1})$, and let $Y_s:=\sum_{u<s}\beta^u\ell_u+\beta^sW(\bm{x}_s)$ for
$s\ge1$. For $s\ge1$, $\bm{x}_s\in X$. Since $\bm{\xi}_{s+1}$ is independent of $\bm{\xi}_{[s]}$ and $\bm{x}_{s+1}$ is a feasible
selection, $\mathbb{E}[Y_{s+1}-Y_s\mid\bm{\xi}_{[s]}]\ge\beta^s(\mathcal{B} W(\bm{x}_s)-W(\bm{x}_s))\ge0$. So $(Y_{s\wedge\sigma})_{s\ge1}$ is a
submartingale, and optional stopping at the bounded time $\sigma$ gives
$\mathcal{B} W(z)\le\mathbb{E}[\ell_0+\beta W(\bm{x}_1)]=\mathbb{E} Y_1\le\mathbb{E} Y_\sigma$. Now $Y_\sigma\le m\bar\ell+\beta^\sigma W(\bm{x}_\sigma)$ and
$W(\bm{x}_\sigma)\le W(y)+L_W\chi$; since $W(y)+L_W\chi\ge0$ and $\sigma\ge1$,
$\mathcal{B} W(z)\le m\bar\ell+\beta(\inf_X W+\epsilon_0+L_W\chi)$. Subtract the lower bound at $x$ and let $\epsilon_0\to0$.

label: rem:lipex
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:lipex}
\emph{Inventory with backlog} (the newsvendor of \citet[eq.~(30)]{julan2023infinite}, with $n=1$): state
$x\in X=[-b',b]$, demand $\xi\ge0$, next state $y\in[\max(-b',x-\xi),b]$, convex ordering, holding and backlog
costs. \ref{Ieta} at $z=b+\eta$ forces $\xi\ge\eta$ a.s., so the rule $\bm{x}_{s+1}=\max(y,\bm{x}_s-\bm{\xi}_{s+1})$ reaches any lower
target $y$, going down by at least $\eta$ per step, and orders reach any higher level in one step: $(R_{m,0})$ holds
with $m=\lceil(b+b')/\eta\rceil+1$. \emph{Hydro reservoir with free spillage}: next level
$y\in[0,\min(b,x+\xi)]$, inflow $\xi\ge0$, convex thermal cost. \ref{Ieta} at $z=-\eta$ forces $\xi\ge\eta$, and the
rule $\bm{x}_{s+1}=\min(y,\bm{x}_s+\bm{\xi}_{s+1})$ gives $(R_{m,0})$ with $m=\lceil b/\eta\rceil+1$. In these examples~\ref{Ieta}
alone gives a $\beta$-uniform bound of order $(D/\eta)\bar\ell/\eta$. Some neighbourhood
condition is needed: $\mathcal{X}(q)=[q,1]$ on $[0,1]$ with loss $q'$ gives $V(q)=q/(1-\beta)$, a Lipschitz constant of order
$1/(1-\beta)$; this example violates feasibility at $q>1$, hence~\ref{Ieta} and Ju--Lan's Assumption~2.2.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:trunc}
Assume \ref{I1}, \cref{ass:S} for $\mathrm{Pb}_H$, and that the normalised stage cuts are $\hat L$-Lipschitz on $X$ (under \ref{Ieta},
with stage cuts valid on $X_\eta$, this holds with $\hat L=\bar\ell/((1-\beta)\eta)$, and with $\hat L=\bar\ell/\eta$ under
$(R_{1,0})$).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item For every $H$ and every $\varepsilon'>0$ with $(1-\beta)\varepsilon'\le\hat\rho$ ($\hat\rho=4\hat L D$),
$\mathbb{E}\,\#\{k\ge1:G^k_H>\varepsilon'\}\le2(d+1)\bar\ell\hat\rho^d/((1-\beta)^{d+2}\varepsilon'^{d+1})$ (\cref{cor:disc}).
\item Let $\bar\pi^k$ be any policy that applies $\pi^{k,H}$ for the first $H$ decisions and then anything
feasible (for instance, restarts $\pi^{k,H}$ every $H$ steps). Then $\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)\le V(x_0)$ and
$V^{\bar\pi^k}(x_0)-V(x_0)\le V^{\bar\pi^k}(x_0)-\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)\le G^k_H+\varepsilon_H$.
\item Hence, for $0<\varepsilon<\bar\ell/(1-\beta)$ with $(1-\beta)\varepsilon\le\hat\rho$ and $H$ as in \cref{thm:det}(ii),
$\mathbb{E}\,\#\{k\ge1:V^{\bar\pi^k}(x_0)-\underline V^{k-1}_{0}(x_0)>\varepsilon\}\le2e(d+1)\bar\ell\hat\rho^d/((1-\beta)^{d+2}\varepsilon^{d+1})$,
with $H$ cuts per iteration (trial-point cuts; the optional cuts of~\ref{O4} are not counted).
\end{enumerate}

body_md:
\label{prop:counter-ih}
Let $x=(u,w)\in[0,1]^2$, $x_0=(0,0)$, deterministic dynamics $\mathcal{X}(u,w)=\{(1-u,w'):0\le w'\le(1+u)/2\}$, loss
$\ell(x,y)=|w-u|+\alpha(1-w')$ with $0<\alpha\le\beta/2$, and $\bar\ell=1+\alpha$; this satisfies~\ref{I1}. Run~(N) with any

$\mathcal V^k_1$ after $k\ge0$ iterations.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item For every exact-cut oracle whose cuts have $w$-slopes in $[-1,1]$ on the slices below (for instance,
subgradients of the natural extension of $\mathcal{B} W$ to $w\in\mathbb{R}$), \cref{cor:disc} applies ($d=1$, $D=1$, $\hat L=1$), so
almost surely $G^k_H\le\varepsilon'$ for all large $k$, for every $\varepsilon'>0$.
\item For every exact-cut oracle that adds, at index~$1$, only the cut at the trial point, and every $k$, $\hat\pi^k$ is the policy $(u,w)\mapsto(1-u,(1+u)/2)$, and
$V^{\hat\pi^k}(x_0)-V(x_0)\ge\beta(\beta-\alpha)/(1-\beta^2)\ge\beta^2/(4(1-\beta))$.
\end{enumerate}

name: Warning: the greedy policy of $\mathcal V_1$ can stay suboptimal

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the slices $X_0=\{x_0\}$, $X_t=\{1\}\times[0,1]$ ($t$ odd) and $\{0\}\times[0,1]$ ($t\ge2$ even): convex, compact,
forward invariant, with $d_t\le1$ and $D_t\le1$. (i) Cuts with $w$-slopes in $[-1,1]$ are $1$-Lipschitz on the slices
(for the natural extension, $\mathcal{B} W(u,w)=|w-u|+\min_{0\le w'\le(1+u)/2}[\alpha(1-w')+\beta W(1-u,w')]$ has $w$-slopes in
$[-1,1]$); apply \cref{cor:disc} and Borel--Cantelli (a finite expected count). (ii) By induction on $k$, suppose $\mathcal V^k_1(1,\cdot)$ is nonincreasing (true
for $k=0$). The first decision minimises $\alpha(1-w_1)+\beta\mathcal V^k_1(1,w_1)$ over $w_1\in[0,1/2]$, a strictly
decreasing function, so $\bm{x}_1=(1,1/2)$. On the slice $\{u=1\}$, $\mathcal{B}\mathcal V_2(1,w)=(1-w)+\mathrm{const}$ is
differentiable at the interior point $w=1/2$, so an affine $f\le\mathcal{B}\mathcal V_2$ on the slice that is tight at $(1,1/2)$
has $w$-slope $-1$, whatever its $u$-slope. Hence $\mathcal V^{k+1}_1=\max(0,\text{cuts})$ is nonincreasing in $w$ on
\emph{every} line $u=\mathrm{const}$, which closes the induction, and at any $(u,w)$ the objective
$\alpha(1-w')+\beta\mathcal V^k_1(1-u,w')$ of $\hat\pi^k$ is strictly decreasing in $w'$, so $w'=(1+u)/2$. From $x_0$, $\hat\pi^k$ alternately visits $(1,\frac12)$ and $(0,1)$, starting with
$(1,\frac12)$, with costs $\alpha/2$ at $t=0$, $1/2$ at odd $t$ and $1+\alpha/2$ at even $t\ge2$, so
$(1-\beta^2)V^{\hat\pi^k}(x_0)=\alpha/2+\beta/2+\beta^2$. The policy that alternates $(0,0)\to(1,\frac12)\to(0,0)$ costs
$\alpha/2$ at even $t$ and $1/2+\alpha$ at odd $t$, so $(1-\beta^2)V(x_0)\le\alpha/2+\beta/2+\beta\alpha$. Subtract, and use
$1+\beta\le2$ and $\alpha\le\beta/2$.

label: prop:tight
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:tight}
Let $X=[0,1]$, $x_0=0$, deterministic dynamics $\mathcal{X}(z)=X$ for all $z\inX_\eta$, loss
$\ell(z,y)=(r_0-az)_++\alpha|y-z|$ with $0<r_0\le a$ and $0<\alpha<\beta a$, and $\underline V^{0}=0$. Then \ref{I1}, \ref{I2}, \ref{Ieta} and
$(R_{1,0})$ hold, and every cut of every possible model is $(a+\alpha)$-Lipschitz, so $\hat L=a+\alpha$ and $D=1$ are
valid. Moreover (i) $\pi^1$ stays at $0$ forever and $G^1=r_0/(1-\beta)$; (ii) $V(x)=(1+\alpha/a)(r_0-ax)_+$ on $X$,
so in variants~(D) and~(G), for every run, $\sup_k\Phi^k\le\operatorname*{avg}_X V=(1+\alpha/a)\,r_0^2/(2a)$. Consequently, if
for some $\vartheta>0$ the bound $\mathbb{E}\sum_{k\ge1}\hat\psi(\vartheta G^k)\le\operatorname*{avg}_X(V-\underline V^{0})$ held for all instances, then
$\vartheta\le2\sqrt2(1+\alpha/a)(1-\beta)$. The same holds for any per-iteration bound
$\mathbb{E}_{k-1}[\Phi^k-\Phi^{k-1}]\ge\hat\psi(\vartheta G^k)$.

name: Tightness of the convex-regret form

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $W$, $\mathcal{B} W(z)=(r_0-az)_++\min_{y\in X}[\alpha|y-z|+\beta W(y)]$ is the sum of an $a$-Lipschitz and an
$\alpha$-Lipschitz function on $X_\eta$, so every subgradient at a point of $X\subset\operatorname{int}X_\eta$ has norm at
most $a+\alpha$. (i) With $\underline V^{0}=0$, the greedy objective is $\alpha|y-x|$, uniquely minimised at $y=x$, so $\bm{x}_t=0$ and
$V^{\pi^1}(0)=r_0/(1-\beta)$. (ii) Let $U(x):=(1+\alpha/a)(r_0-ax)_+$. For $x\ge r_0/a$, $y=x$ gives $\mathcal{B} U(x)=0=U(x)$. For
$x<r_0/a$: on $y\in[x,r_0/a]$ the objective $\alpha(y-x)+\beta(a+\alpha)(r_0/a-y)$ is decreasing, since
$\alpha<\beta(a+\alpha)$; on $y\ge r_0/a$ it is increasing, and on $y\le x$ it is decreasing in $y$. So the minimum is
$\alpha(r_0/a-x)$, and $\mathcal{B} U(x)=r_0-ax+\alpha(r_0/a-x)=U(x)$. Hence $U=V$, and $\Phi^k\le\operatorname*{avg} V$ by \cref{lem:validIH}(a).
The average is $(1+\alpha/a)\int_0^{r_0/a}(r_0-as)\,ds$. \emph{Consequence.} Here $\hat\rho=4(a+\alpha)$, and the $k=1$
term alone gives $\hat\psi(s)\le(1+\alpha/a)r_0^2/(2a)$ with $s:=\vartheta r_0/(1-\beta)$. If $s>\hat\rho$, then
$\hat\psi(s)>\hat\psi(\hat\rho)=a+\alpha>(1+\alpha/a)a/2\ge(1+\alpha/a)r_0^2/(2a)$, a contradiction. So $s\le\hat\rho$, and
$s^2/(4\hat\rho)\le(1+\alpha/a)r_0^2/(2a)$ gives $\vartheta^2\le8(1+\alpha/a)^2(1-\beta)^2$.
